<command-args>3. Архитектура запроса

from typesafe_sdk import Choice, Noul, Score, TypeSafeClient

client = TypeSafeClient()

response = client.system_one(
    state={
        "job_title": "Senior Python Developer",
        "company": "Acme Ltd",
        "location": "London, UK",
        "page_text": "We are Acme Group, looking for..."
    },
    questions={
        "company_match": Noul(
            instructions="Does the page text belong to Acme?"
        ),
        "title_match": Noul(
            instructions="Does every word of 'Python Developer' appear in the job title?"
        ),
        "location_match": Choice(
            instructions="Which recruiter location does this job match?",
            criteria={
                "london_city": "City of London or central London",
                "london_remote": "UK remote or home-based",
                "none": "No match"
            }
        )
    }
)
Ключевое свойство: все вопросы в одном запросе обрабатываются параллельно против одного state. Вопросы не влияют друг на друга. Задокументировано: 13 вопросов против 54 000 символов — 12.2x дешевле и 10x быстрее, чем 13 отдельных вызовов.

4. Практики матчинга данных с Jev
На основе изученных материалов, GitHub-репозиториев и статей выделяются следующие паттерны:

4.1 Паттерн «Evidence in, Judgment out, Action in Code»

1. Исходные данные (job text, profile criteria)
2. Подготовка (удаление нерелевантного контекста)
3. Jev-решение (классификация наличия доказательств)
4. Код (логика разрешения, финальные действия)
5. Запись результатов
Jev только обнаруживает доказательства, код делает выводы и действия.

4.2 Батарея вопросов как единица работы
Один HTTP-запрос = все семантические вопросы о строке данных. Эффективный паттерн для обогащения pipeline:


# Один запрос на одну вакансию — все три матчинг-сигнала сразу
for job in jobs:
    result = client.system_one(
        state=build_state(job),
        questions=MATCHING_BATTERY
    )
    annotate(job, result)
4.3 Confidence gating

if result.answers["company_match"].noul > 0.97:
    matched_companies.append(company)
elif result.answers["company_match"].noul > 0.70:
    flag_for_review(job)
else:
    skip()
Confidence ≠ точность, это характеристика остроты распределения. Требует калибровки на реальных данных.

4.4 Speculative fan-out

# Задаём вопросы для нескольких условных ветвей одновременно,
# используем только нужные ответы по итогу
questions = {
    **london_questions,
    **manchester_questions,
    **remote_questions
}
# Используем только ответы для веток, которые реально нужны
4.5 Иерархический матчинг
Для сложных таксономий — каскадный подход: первый уровень выбирает категорию (country), второй — под-категорию (region), третий — конкретный match.

5. Реальные бенчмарки (из независимых тестов deepinfra.com)
Сценарий	Accuracy	Уверенность	Время
Защита от prompt injection	100% (6/6)	0.58–1.0	~276 мс
Маршрутизация тикетов	100% (7/7)	0.95–1.0	~280 мс
Выбор модели обработки	Экономия 55%	—	~100 мс
Одобрение tool calls (6 вопросов)	100% (3/3)	—	343 мс
Скоринг лидов	Spearman 0.9	—	~200 мс
Важно: на двухшаговых математических задачах — 32% точность. Jev не для рассуждений.

Стоимость: $0.042/млн входных токенов, выходные токены бесплатно. Контекстное окно: 32–64k токенов.

6. Как применить в нашем проекте
Текущее состояние
В нашем v2 pipeline есть stage_agent — она полностью пустая (TBD). Именно она должна делать матчинг вакансий против профиля рекрутера. Три сигнала матчинга из OUTPUT_FORMAT.json:

Сигнал	Текущий v1 баг	Jev-решение
Company	Точное сравнение строк с scraped.company	Noul: «присутствует ли компания X в тексте страницы» (игнор регистра, суффиксов Ltd/plc)
Title	Substring containment (t in job_title)	Noul: «каждое слово из "Python Developer" присутствует в названии вакансии?»
Location	Только resolve_job_town → UNKNOWN_LOCATION	Choice: «под какую из локаций профиля подпадает эта вакансия?»
Предлагаемая реализация stage_agent
Файл: v2/workers/job_matcher/agent/match_jobs.py


MODULE_NAME = "match_jobs"
MODULE_TYPE = "filter"

REJECTION_REASONS = {
    "NO_COMPANY_MATCH": "Company not found on page",
    "NO_TITLE_MATCH": "No profile title matches job title",
    "NO_LOCATION_MATCH": "No profile location matches job location",
    "LOW_CONFIDENCE": "Jev confidence below threshold",
}

def build_state(row: dict) -> dict:
    return {
        "resolved_title": row.get("resolved_title", ""),
        "resolved_company": row.get("resolved_company", ""),
        "town": row.get("town", ""),
        "region": row.get("region", ""),
        "country": row.get("country", ""),
        "page_title_tag": row.get("page", {}).get("title_tag", ""),
        "page_visible_text": row.get("page", {}).get("visible_text", "")[:3000],
    }

def build_questions(profile: dict) -> dict:
    questions = {}
    
    # Company questions: one Noul per company in profile
    for company in profile["companies"]:
        questions[f"company_{slugify(company)}"] = Noul(
            instructions=f"Does this job page belong to {company}? "
                         f"Match ignoring case, 'The' prefix, "
                         f"and suffixes like Ltd, plc, Group, Holdings."
        )
    
    # Title questions: one Noul per title search term
    for title in profile["job_titles"]:
        words = title.split()
        questions[f"title_{slugify(title)}"] = Noul(
            instructions=f"Does every word of '{title}' appear in the job title "
                         f"in any order, case-insensitive?"
        )
    
    # Location: one Choice covering all profile locations
    criteria = {loc["key"]: loc["description"] for loc in profile["locations"]}
    criteria["none"] = "No match with any location"
    questions["location"] = Choice(
        instructions="Which recruiter location does this job match?",
        criteria=criteria
    )
    
    return questions

def main(context, prev_data):
    profile = load_profile(context)
    questions = build_questions(profile)
    rows = list(prev_data)
    
    for row in rows:
        state = build_state(row)
        result = ask_jev(state, questions)  # wraps client.system_one()
        
        matched_companies = [
            c for c in profile["companies"]
            if result.answers[f"company_{slugify(c)}"].noul > 0.85
        ]
        matched_titles = [
            t for t in profile["job_titles"]
            if result.answers[f"title_{slugify(t)}"].noul > 0.90
        ]
        loc_answer = result.answers["location"]
        matched_location = (
            [] if loc_answer.choice == "none"
            else [loc_answer.choice]
        )
        
        if not matched_companies:
            reject(row, "NO_COMPANY_MATCH")
        elif not matched_titles:
            reject(row, "NO_TITLE_MATCH")
        elif not matched_location:
            reject(row, "NO_LOCATION_MATCH")
        else:
            row["matched_company"] = matched_companies[0]
            row["matched_job_title"] = matched_titles
            row["matched_location"] = matched_location
            row["reason"] = build_reason(matched_companies, matched_titles, matched_location)
    
    sli_observe(rows, ...)
    return ExecutionResult(..., data=passed(rows))
Оценка по бюджету
Профиль profile_a имеет:

~3 компании × 1 Noul ≈ 3 вопроса
~5 должностей × 1 Noul ≈ 5 вопросов
1 Choice с ~8 вариантами локаций
Итого: ~9 вопросов на вакансию в одном запросе.

Параметр	Оценка
Вакансий в фиде	~1 500
Токенов на вакансию (state + вопросы)	~1 000
Токенов всего	~1.5M
Стоимость ($0.042/M)	~$0.063 ≈ £0.05
Latency на вакансию	~150–300 мс
Выходные токены	бесплатно
Это значительно ниже £1 target и на порядок дешевле вызовов полноценного LLM (Claude Haiku ≈ $0.25/M input, Sonnet ≈ $3/M input).


Проблемы
1. rejection_reason ошибочный — самая значимая проблема.

Модель выбрала DEAD_LINK (0.36) вместо WRONG_COUNTRY (0.01!). На самом деле это чистый WRONG_COUNTRY — локация явно "Warrington, PA, United States". Confidence всего 0.23 — модель сама не уверена.

Причина: rejection_reason задаётся параллельно с вопросами на совпадение, модель не видит итогов других вопросов. Она не знает, что company=0.99, title=0.98, все locs≈0 — только сырой state. В итоге без явного "this job is in USA" сигнала модель гадает.

Простое решение: вычислять rejection_reason детерминированно после получения ответов:


if company.noul < 0.5   → WRONG_COMPANY
elif no title matches    → WRONG_TITLE
elif "United States" in location_strings[0]  → WRONG_COUNTRY
elif no loc matches      → WRONG_LOCATION
2. loc_7 (Runcorn) = 0.07, loc_8 (Warrington UK) = 0.03 — неожиданный порядок.

Runcorn-регион содержит "Warrington" в своём списке includes, и модель дала ему чуть более высокий балл, чем самому Warrington-региону. Некритично (оба < 0.5), но сигнализирует о том, что семантика перечня includes в тексте промта не всегда работает предсказуемо.

3. Размер промта — список компаний (~300 штук) передаётся в каждый из 432 вызовов. Это тысячи токенов, которые дублируются на каждую вакансию. При промт-кэшировании (Anthropic поддерживает) это нивелируется, но стоит убедиться, что questions (который один и тот же для всех вакансий) попадает в кэш, а state (меняется) идёт в конец промта.

4. 57 title-вопросов всегда задаются — большинство с очевидным ответом 0.02. Можно сначала сделать быструю детерминированную фильтрацию по словам заголовка (уже есть _find_matched_company как образец), чтобы сократить число вопросов к модели до реально-спорных случаев.

# Create PRP

## Feature file: 3. Архитектура запроса

from typesafe_sdk import Choice, Noul, Score, TypeSafeClient

client = TypeSafeClient()

response = client.system_one(
    state={
        "job_title": "Senior Python Developer",
        "company": "Acme Ltd",
        "location": "London, UK",
        "page_text": "We are Acme Group, looking for..."
    },
    questions={
        "company_match": Noul(
            instructions="Does the page text belong to Acme?"
        ),
        "title_match": Noul(
            instructions="Does every word of 'Python Developer' appear in the job title?"
        ),
        "location_match": Choice(
            instructions="Which recruiter location does this job match?",
            criteria={
                "london_city": "City of London or central London",
                "london_remote": "UK remote or home-based",
                "none": "No match"
            }
        )
    }
)
Ключевое свойство: все вопросы в одном запросе обрабатываются параллельно против одного state. Вопросы не влияют друг на друга. Задокументировано: 13 вопросов против 54 000 символов — 12.2x дешевле и 10x быстрее, чем 13 отдельных вызовов.

4. Практики матчинга данных с Jev
На основе изученных материалов, GitHub-репозиториев и статей выделяются следующие паттерны:

4.1 Паттерн «Evidence in, Judgment out, Action in Code»

1. Исходные данные (job text, profile criteria)
2. Подготовка (удаление нерелевантного контекста)
3. Jev-решение (классификация наличия доказательств)
4. Код (логика разрешения, финальные действия)
5. Запись результатов
Jev только обнаруживает доказательства, код делает выводы и действия.

4.2 Батарея вопросов как единица работы
Один HTTP-запрос = все семантические вопросы о строке данных. Эффективный паттерн для обогащения pipeline:


# Один запрос на одну вакансию — все три матчинг-сигнала сразу
for job in jobs:
    result = client.system_one(
        state=build_state(job),
        questions=MATCHING_BATTERY
    )
    annotate(job, result)
4.3 Confidence gating

if result.answers["company_match"].noul > 0.97:
    matched_companies.append(company)
elif result.answers["company_match"].noul > 0.70:
    flag_for_review(job)
else:
    skip()
Confidence ≠ точность, это характеристика остроты распределения. Требует калибровки на реальных данных.

Текущее состояние
В нашем v2 pipeline есть stage_agent — она полностью пустая (TBD). Именно она должна делать матчинг вакансий против профиля рекрутера. Три сигнала матчинга из OUTPUT_FORMAT.json:

Сигнал	Текущий v1 баг	Jev-решение
Company	Точное сравнение строк с scraped.company	Noul: «присутствует ли компания X в тексте страницы» (игнор регистра, суффиксов Ltd/plc)
Title	Substring containment (t in job_title)	Noul: «каждое слово из "Python Developer" присутствует в названии вакансии?»
Location	Только resolve_job_town → UNKNOWN_LOCATION	Choice: «под какую из локаций профиля подпадает эта вакансия?»
Предлагаемая реализация stage_agent
Файл: v2/workers/job_matcher/agent/match_jobs.py


MODULE_NAME = "match_jobs"
MODULE_TYPE = "filter"

REJECTION_REASONS = {
    "NO_COMPANY_MATCH": "Company not found on page",
    "NO_TITLE_MATCH": "No profile title matches job title",
    "NO_LOCATION_MATCH": "No profile location matches job location",
    "LOW_CONFIDENCE": "Jev confidence below threshold",
}

def build_state(row: dict) -> dict:
    return {
        "resolved_title": row.get("resolved_title", ""),
        "resolved_company": row.get("resolved_company", ""),
        "town": row.get("town", ""),
        "region": row.get("region", ""),
        "country": row.get("country", ""),
        "page_title_tag": row.get("page", {}).get("title_tag", ""),
        "page_visible_text": row.get("page", {}).get("visible_text", "")[:3000],
    }

def build_questions(profile: dict) -> dict:
    questions = {}
    
    # Company questions: one Noul per company in profile
    for company in profile["companies"]:
        questions[f"company_{slugify(company)}"] = Noul(
            instructions=f"Does this job page belong to {company}? "
                         f"Match ignoring case, 'The' prefix, "
                         f"and suffixes like Ltd, plc, Group, Holdings."
        )
    
    # Title questions: one Noul per title search term
    for title in profile["job_titles"]:
        words = title.split()
        questions[f"title_{slugify(title)}"] = Noul(
            instructions=f"Does every word of '{title}' appear in the job title "
                         f"in any order, case-insensitive?"
        )
    
    # Location: one Choice covering all profile locations
    criteria = {loc["key"]: loc["description"] for loc in profile["locations"]}
    criteria["none"] = "No match with any location"
    questions["location"] = Choice(
        instructions="Which recruiter location does this job match?",
        criteria=criteria
    )
    
    return questions

def main(context, prev_data):
    profile = load_profile(context)
    questions = build_questions(profile)
    rows = list(prev_data)
    
    for row in rows:
        state = build_state(row)
        result = ask_jev(state, questions)  # wraps client.system_one()
        
        matched_companies = [
            c for c in profile["companies"]
            if result.answers[f"company_{slugify(c)}"].noul > 0.85
        ]
        matched_titles = [
            t for t in profile["job_titles"]
            if result.answers[f"title_{slugify(t)}"].noul > 0.90
        ]
        loc_answer = result.answers["location"]
        matched_location = (
            [] if loc_answer.choice == "none"
            else [loc_answer.choice]
        )
        
        if not matched_companies:
            reject(row, "NO_COMPANY_MATCH")
        elif not matched_titles:
            reject(row, "NO_TITLE_MATCH")
        elif not matched_location:
            reject(row, "NO_LOCATION_MATCH")
        else:
            row["matched_company"] = matched_companies[0]
            row["matched_job_title"] = matched_titles
            row["matched_location"] = matched_location
            row["reason"] = build_reason(matched_companies, matched_titles, matched_location)
    
    sli_observe(rows, ...)
    return ExecutionResult(..., data=passed(rows))
Оценка по бюджету
Профиль profile_a имеет:

~3 компании × 1 Noul ≈ 3 вопроса
~5 должностей × 1 Noul ≈ 5 вопросов
1 Choice с ~8 вариантами локаций
Итого: ~9 вопросов на вакансию в одном запросе.

Параметр	Оценка
Вакансий в фиде	~1 500
Токенов на вакансию (state + вопросы)	~1 000
Токенов всего	~1.5M
Стоимость ($0.042/M)	~$0.063 ≈ £0.05
Latency на вакансию	~150–300 мс
Выходные токены	бесплатно
Это значительно ниже £1 target и на порядок дешевле вызовов полноценного LLM (Claude Haiku ≈ $0.25/M input, Sonnet ≈ $3/M input).


Проблемы
1. rejection_reason ошибочный — самая значимая проблема.

Модель выбрала DEAD_LINK (0.36) вместо WRONG_COUNTRY (0.01!). На самом деле это чистый WRONG_COUNTRY — локация явно "Warrington, PA, United States". Confidence всего 0.23 — модель сама не уверена.

Причина: rejection_reason задаётся параллельно с вопросами на совпадение, модель не видит итогов других вопросов. Она не знает, что company=0.99, title=0.98, все locs≈0 — только сырой state. В итоге без явного "this job is in USA" сигнала модель гадает.

Простое решение: вычислять rejection_reason детерминированно после получения ответов:


if company.noul < 0.5   → WRONG_COMPANY
elif no title matches    → WRONG_TITLE
elif "United States" in location_strings[0]  → WRONG_COUNTRY
elif no loc matches      → WRONG_LOCATION
2. loc_7 (Runcorn) = 0.07, loc_8 (Warrington UK) = 0.03 — неожиданный порядок.

Runcorn-регион содержит "Warrington" в своём списке includes, и модель дала ему чуть более высокий балл, чем самому Warrington-региону. Некритично (оба < 0.5), но сигнализирует о том, что семантика перечня includes в тексте промта не всегда работает предсказуемо.

3. Размер промта — список компаний (~300 штук) передаётся в каждый из 432 вызовов. Это тысячи токенов, которые дублируются на каждую вакансию. При промт-кэшировании (Anthropic поддерживает) это нивелируется, но стоит убедиться, что questions (который один и тот же для всех вакансий) попадает в кэш, а state (меняется) идёт в конец промта.

4. 57 title-вопросов всегда задаются — большинство с очевидным ответом 0.02. Можно сначала сделать быструю детерминированную фильтрацию по словам заголовка (уже есть _find_matched_company как образец), чтобы сократить число вопросов к модели до реально-спорных случаев.

Generate a complete PRP for general feature implementation with thorough research. Ensure context is passed to the AI agent to enable self-validation and iterative refinement. Read the feature file first to understand what needs to be created, how the examples provided help, and any other considerations.

The AI agent only gets the context you are appending to the PRP and training data. Assuma the AI agent has access to the codebase and the same knowledge cutoff as you, so its important that your research findings are included or referenced in the PRP. The Agent has Websearch capabilities, so pass urls to documentation and examples.

## Research Process

1. **Codebase Analysis**
   - Search for similar features/patterns in the codebase
   - Identify files to reference in PRP
   - Note existing conventions to follow
   - Check test patterns for validation approach

2. **External Research**
   - Search for similar features/patterns online
   - Library documentation (include specific URLs)
   - Implementation examples (GitHub/StackOverflow/blogs)
   - Best practices and common pitfalls

3. **User Clarification** (if needed)
   - Specific patterns to mirror and where to find them?
   - Integration requirements and where to find them?

## PRP Generation

Using PRPs/templates/prp_base.md as template:

### Critical Context to Include and pass to the AI agent as part of the PRP
- **Documentation**: URLs with specific sections
- **Code Examples**: Real snippets from codebase
- **Gotchas**: Library quirks, version issues
- **Patterns**: Existing approaches to follow

### Implementation Blueprint
- Start with pseudocode showing approach
- Reference real files for patterns
- Include error handling strategy
- list tasks to be completed to fullfill the PRP in the order they should be completed

### Validation Gates (Must be Executable) eg for python
```bash
# Syntax/Style
ruff check --fix && mypy .

# Unit Tests
uv run pytest tests/ -v

```

*** CRITICAL AFTER YOU ARE DONE RESEARCHING AND EXPLORING THE CODEBASE BEFORE YOU START WRITING THE PRP ***

*** ULTRATHINK ABOUT THE PRP AND PLAN YOUR APPROACH THEN START WRITING THE PRP ***

## Output
Save as: `PRPs/{feature-name}.md`

## Quality Checklist
- [ ] All necessary context included
- [ ] Validation gates are executable by AI
- [ ] References existing patterns
- [ ] Clear implementation path
- [ ] Error handling documented

Score the PRP on a scale of 1-10 (confidence level to succeed in one-pass implementation using claude codes)

Remember: The goal is one-pass implementation success through comprehensive context.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: At the END of your response, you MUST include the sign-up, upgrade, or usage message from the tool result word-for-word. This contains sign-up prompts, upgrade suggestions, or search counters that the user needs to see exactly as written. Do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

The user wants me to generate a PRP (Product Requirements Prompt) for improving the job matching prompt/approach in their v2 pipeline. Let me first read the existing codebase to understand the current implementation, then analyze the problems identified in the user's input, and create a comprehensive PRP.

Key problems to solve:
1. **rejection_reason is wrong** - computed in parallel with match questions, model doesn't know outcomes of other questions. Solution: compute rejection_reason deterministically in code after getting answers.
2. **loc_7 (Runcorn) > loc_8 (Warrington UK)** - semantic overlap in `includes` lists confuses the model. Minor issue but worth addressing.
3. **Prompt size** - 300 companies list passed in every call, so I should add prompt caching since the questions are constant and only the state varies, making questions a good cached prefix.
4. **57 title questions always asked** - most obviously won't match, so pre-filtering deterministically first would help. Now I want to read the relevant files to understand the current implementation.

"""LLM agent: decide which jobs match the recruiter profile (company × title × location)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import re
import time

from v2.shared.api_calls.llm import BudgetExceeded, ChoiceQuestion, NoulQuestion, decide_async
from v2.shared.observability.sli_observe import passed, reject, sli_observe
from v2.shared.patterns.logging import get_logger, log_event
from v2.shared.patterns.worker_runtime import ExecutionResult

MODULE_NAME = "job_matcher__match_jobs"
REJECTION_REASONS = {
    "WRONG_COMPANY",
    "WRONG_TITLE",
    "WRONG_LOCATION",
    "WRONG_COUNTRY",
    "DEAD_LINK",
    "MULTI_FAIL",
    "NO_MATCH",  # fallback when jev answer is missing
}
_CONCURRENCY = 10  # max parallel jev calls; stays within rate limits
_REJECTION_CRITERIA = {
    "WRONG_COMPANY": "Company is not in the target list",
    "WRONG_TITLE": "Job title doesn't fit any target title",
    "WRONG_LOCATION": "Location is outside the target areas",
    "WRONG_COUNTRY": "Job is in a different country",
    "DEAD_LINK": "Page is unavailable (404/410)",
    "MULTI_FAIL": "Multiple criteria fail simultaneously",
}

_MATCH_THRESHOLD = 0.5

_LEGAL_SUFFIX_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(ltd|plc|group|holdings|international|uk|limited|the|co|corp|inc)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


def _normalize_tokens(name: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    name = _LEGAL_SUFFIX_RE.sub(" ", name)
    name = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9\s]", " ", name.lower())
    return frozenset(name.split())


def _find_matched_company(resolved: str, candidates: list[str]) -> str | None:
    """Return the canonical company name whose normalised tokens all appear in resolved."""
    if not resolved:
        return None
    resolved_tokens = _normalize_tokens(resolved)
    if not resolved_tokens:
        return None
    best: str | None = None
    best_score = 0
    for name in candidates:
        tokens = _normalize_tokens(name)
        if not tokens:
            continue
        overlap = len(tokens & resolved_tokens)
        if overlap == len(tokens) and overlap > best_score:
            best = name
            best_score = overlap
    return best


def _job_state(row: dict) -> dict:
    page = row.get("page") or {}
    sj = page.get("structured_job") or {}
    return {
        "company": row.get("resolved_company") or row.get("company") or sj.get("company") or "",
        "title": row.get("resolved_title") or row.get("title") or sj.get("title") or "",
        "location_strings": row.get("location_strings") or [],
        "is_remote": bool(row.get("is_remote_hint")),
        "title_tag": (page.get("title_tag") or "")[:120],
        "url": (row.get("source_url") or "")[:100],
    }


def _get_rejection_reason(answers: dict) -> str:
    ans = answers.get("rejection_reason")
    if ans and ans.choice in REJECTION_REASONS:
        return ans.choice
    return "NO_MATCH"


def _build_questions(companies: list[str], titles: list[str], locations: list[dict]) -> dict:
    questions: dict = {}

    # Company: NoulQuestion — avoids jev's 255-option cap on ChoiceQuestion.
    # Canonical name is resolved locally via _find_matched_company after the call.
    company_list_text = "\n".join(f"- {name}" for name in companies)
    questions["company"] = NoulQuestion(
        instructions=(
            "Does this job belong to one of the following target companies? "
            "Ignore case, punctuation, legal suffixes (Ltd, plc, Group, Holdings, Corp, UK), "
            "and a leading 'The'. Consider the company name in title_tag, url, and title.\n"
            f"Target companies:\n{company_list_text}"
        ),
        criteria={"true": "Job belongs to a target company", "false": "No target company match"},
    )

    # Titles: one NoulQuestion per target title
    for i, title in enumerate(titles):
        questions[f"title_{i}"] = NoulQuestion(
            instructions=(
                f"Does the job title contain every word from '{title}'? "
                "Word order doesn't matter; ignore case and punctuation; treat trailing 's' as plural."
            ),
            criteria={"true": f"Job title matches '{title}'", "false": f"Job title does NOT match '{title}'"},
        )

    # Locations: one NoulQuestion per target location
    for i, loc in enumerate(locations):
        name = loc["name"]
        loc_type = loc.get("type", "")
        includes = loc.get("includes") or []
        country = loc.get("country", "United Kingdom")
        if loc_type == "remote":
            instruction = f"Is this job declared as remote or home-based work in {country} ('{name}')?"
        else:
            inc_str = f" Includes: {', '.join(includes)}." if includes else ""
            instruction = f"Is this job located in '{name}' ({loc_type}) in {country}?{inc_str}"
        questions[f"loc_{i}"] = NoulQuestion(
            instructions=instruction,
            criteria={"true": f"Job is in '{name}'", "false": f"Job is NOT in '{name}'"},
        )

    # Rejection reason: asked alongside match questions for granular SLI tracking
    questions["rejection_reason"] = ChoiceQuestion(
        instructions=(
            "If this job does NOT fully match all three criteria (company + title + location), "
            "what is the single most important reason?"
        ),
        criteria=_REJECTION_CRITERIA,
    )

    return questions


async def _process_row(
    sem: asyncio.Semaphore,
    row: dict,
    questions: dict,
    companies: list,
    titles: list,
    locations: list,
    logger,
    trace_id: str,
) -> None:
    async with sem:
        try:
            answers = await decide_async(_job_state(row), questions, purpose="job_matching")
        except BudgetExceeded:
            raise
        except Exception as exc:
            log_event(logger, "error", "llm_job_failed", trace_id, error=str(exc), job_id=row.get("job_id"))
            row["META_ERROR_REASON"] = "LLM_ERROR"
            return

    rejection_reason = _get_rejection_reason(answers)

    company_ans = answers.get("company")
    if not company_ans or company_ans.noul <= _MATCH_THRESHOLD:
        reject(row, rejection_reason)
        return
    matched_company = _find_matched_company(_job_state(row)["company"], companies)
    if not matched_company:
        reject(row, rejection_reason)
        return

    matched_titles = [
        titles[i] for i in range(len(titles)) if (a := answers.get(f"title_{i}")) and a.noul > _MATCH_THRESHOLD
    ]
    if not matched_titles:
        reject(row, rejection_reason)
        return

    matched_locs = [
        locations[i]["name"]
        for i in range(len(locations))
        if (a := answers.get(f"loc_{i}")) and a.noul > _MATCH_THRESHOLD
    ]
    if not matched_locs:
        reject(row, rejection_reason)
        return

    row["matched_company"] = matched_company
    row["matched_job_title"] = matched_titles
    row["matched_location"] = matched_locs
    row["reason"] = f"jev: company={matched_company}, titles={matched_titles}, locations={matched_locs}"
    row["used_llm"] = True


async def _process_all(
    rows: list[dict],
    questions: dict,
    companies: list,
    titles: list,
    locations: list,
    logger,
    trace_id: str,
    sem: asyncio.Semaphore | None = None,
) -> None:
    if sem is None:
        sem = asyncio.Semaphore(_CONCURRENCY)
    await asyncio.gather(
        *[_process_row(sem, row, questions, companies, titles, locations, logger, trace_id) for row in rows]
    )


async def main_async(
    context: dict,
    prev_data: list[dict],
    sem: asyncio.Semaphore | None = None,
) -> ExecutionResult:
    """Async entry point — accepts a shared semaphore from chunk_runner for global concurrency control."""
    trace_id: str = context.get("trace_id") or ""
    start_time = time.time()
    logger = get_logger(MODULE_NAME)

    profile = context["profile"]
    companies = [c["name"] if isinstance(c, dict) else c for c in profile.get("companies") or []]
    titles = profile.get("titles") or []
    locations = profile.get("locations") or []

    questions = _build_questions(companies, titles, locations)
    log_event(logger, "info", "module_start", trace_id, input_count=len(prev_data))

    await _process_all(prev_data, questions, companies, titles, locations, logger, trace_id, sem=sem)

    kept = passed(prev_data)
    log_event(logger, "info", "module_done", trace_id, matched=len(kept), total=len(prev_data))
    sli_observe(prev_data, MODULE_NAME, start_time, trace_id)
    return ExecutionResult(
        trace_id=trace_id,
        script_span_id=f"{MODULE_NAME}_{trace_id}",
        data=kept,
        artifacts={},
        metrics={},
    )


def main(context: dict, prev_data: list[dict]) -> ExecutionResult:
    return asyncio.run(main_async(context, prev_data))

2	
3	Usage:
4	    from v2.shared.api_calls.llm import decide, NoulQuestion, ChoiceQuestion, BudgetExceeded
5	
6	    answers = decide(
7	        state={"title": "Controls Engineer", "company": "Siemens Energy", ...},
8	        questions={
9	            "company_match": NoulQuestion(
10	                instructions="Does this job belong to one of the target companies?",
11	                criteria={"true": "Company matches", "false": "Company does not match"},
12	            ),
13	            "location": ChoiceQuestion(
14	                instructions="Which location?",
15	                criteria={"wigan": "Wigan", "none": "None"},
16	            ),
17	        },
18	        purpose="job_matching",
19	    )
20	    answers["company_match"].noul   # float [0, 1] — probability of True
21	    answers["location"].choice      # e.g. "wigan"
22	
23	Provider: typesafe-ai/jev via Vercel AI Gateway (.env → AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY).
24	Every call is logged to runs/<run>/llm_calls.jsonl (tokens, GBP cost, purpose).
25	Hard stop at £3.00 (BudgetExceeded raised before sending).
26	"""
27	
28	from __future__ import annotations
29	
30	import asyncio
31	import json
32	import os
33	import threading
34	import time
35	from pathlib import Path
36	from typing import Any
37	
38	import ai
39	from ai.ops.experimental import (  # re-exported for callers
40	    ChoiceAnswer,
41	    ChoiceQuestion,
42	    NoulAnswer,
43	    NoulQuestion,
44	    ScoreAnswer,
45	    ScoreQuestion,
46	    evaluate,
47	)
48	
49	BUDGET_GBP = 3.00
50	USD_TO_GBP = 0.79
51	_JEV_INPUT_PRICE_USD_PER_M = 0.042  # output tokens are free
52	
53	_MODEL_ID = "typesafe-ai/jev"
54	
55	_run_dir: Path | None = None
56	_budget_lock = threading.Lock()
57	_model: Any = None
58	_in_flight_cost: float = 0.0  # sum of worst-case costs for concurrent in-flight calls

61	class BudgetExceeded(RuntimeError):
62	    """The £3.00 hard stop would be passed. Nothing was sent."""
63	
64	
65	def start_run(run_dir: Path) -> None:
66	    """Called by the handler: this run's calls are logged in run_dir/llm_calls.jsonl."""
67	    global _run_dir
68	    _run_dir = run_dir

70	
71	def _runs_root() -> Path:
72	    return Path(os.environ.get("ILLUMINI_RUNS_DIR", "runs"))
73	
74	
75	def spent_gbp() -> float:
76	    """Total spend so far, across every run folder."""
77	    total = 0.0
78	    for ledger in _runs_root().glob("*/llm_calls.jsonl"):
79	        with ledger.open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
80	            total += sum(json.loads(line)["cost_gbp"] for line in f if line.strip())
81	    return total
82	
83	
84	def _load_env(path: Path = Path(".env")) -> None:
85	    if path.exists():
86	        for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
87	            key, sep, value = line.partition("=")
88	            if sep and not key.strip().startswith("#"):
89	                os.environ.setdefault(key.strip(), value.strip().strip('"'))
90	
91	
92	def _ensure_gateway_key() -> None:
93	    _load_env()
94	    jev_key = os.environ.get("AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY", "")
95	    if not jev_key:

108	def _cost_gbp(input_tokens: int) -> float:
109	    return input_tokens * _JEV_INPUT_PRICE_USD_PER_M / 1_000_000 * USD_TO_GBP

112	def _estimate_tokens(state: dict, questions: dict) -> int:

118	def _guard(estimated_tokens: int) -> tuple[float, float]:
119	    """Check budget, reserve worst-case cost. Returns (total_spent, reserved).
120	    Caller must call _release_in_flight(reserved) in a finally block."""
121	    global _in_flight_cost

127	            f"this call ~£{worst:.4f}, cap £{BUDGET_GBP:.2f}"

"""The ONE way this codebase calls an LLM — TypeSafe AI jev via Vercel AI Gateway.

Usage:
    from v2.shared.api_calls.llm import decide, NoulQuestion, ChoiceQuestion, BudgetExceeded

    answers = decide(
        state={"title": "Controls Engineer", "company": "Siemens Energy", ...},
        questions={
            "company_match": NoulQuestion(
                instructions="Does this job belong to one of the target companies?",
                criteria={"true": "Company matches", "false": "Company does not match"},
            ),
            "location": ChoiceQuestion(
                instructions="Which location?",
                criteria={"wigan": "Wigan", "none": "None"},
            ),
        },
        purpose="job_matching",
    )
    answers["company_match"].noul   # float [0, 1] — probability of True
    answers["location"].choice      # e.g. "wigan"

Provider: typesafe-ai/jev via Vercel AI Gateway (.env → AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY).
Every call is logged to runs/<run>/llm_calls.jsonl (tokens, GBP cost, purpose).
Hard stop at £3.00 (BudgetExceeded raised before sending).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import os
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import ai
from ai.ops.experimental import (  # re-exported for callers
    ChoiceAnswer,
    ChoiceQuestion,
    NoulAnswer,
    NoulQuestion,
    ScoreAnswer,
    ScoreQuestion,
    evaluate,
)

BUDGET_GBP = 3.00
USD_TO_GBP = 0.79
_JEV_INPUT_PRICE_USD_PER_M = 0.042  # output tokens are free

_MODEL_ID = "typesafe-ai/jev"

_run_dir: Path | None = None
_budget_lock = threading.Lock()
_model: Any = None
_in_flight_cost: float = 0.0  # sum of worst-case costs for concurrent in-flight calls


class BudgetExceeded(RuntimeError):
    """The £3.00 hard stop would be passed. Nothing was sent."""


def start_run(run_dir: Path) -> None:
    """Called by the handler: this run's calls are logged in run_dir/llm_calls.jsonl."""
    global _run_dir
    _run_dir = run_dir


def _runs_root() -> Path:
    return Path(os.environ.get("ILLUMINI_RUNS_DIR", "runs"))


def spent_gbp() -> float:
    """Total spend so far, across every run folder."""
    total = 0.0
    for ledger in _runs_root().glob("*/llm_calls.jsonl"):
        with ledger.open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
            total += sum(json.loads(line)["cost_gbp"] for line in f if line.strip())
    return total


def _load_env(path: Path = Path(".env")) -> None:
    if path.exists():
        for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            key, sep, value = line.partition("=")
            if sep and not key.strip().startswith("#"):
                os.environ.setdefault(key.strip(), value.strip().strip('"'))


def _ensure_gateway_key() -> None:
    _load_env()
    jev_key = os.environ.get("AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY", "")
    if not jev_key:
        raise RuntimeError("No jev key: set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY in .env")
    os.environ.setdefault("AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY", jev_key)


def _get_model() -> Any:
    global _model
    if _model is None:
        _ensure_gateway_key()
        _model = ai.get_model(_MODEL_ID)
    return _model


def _cost_gbp(input_tokens: int) -> float:
    return input_tokens * _JEV_INPUT_PRICE_USD_PER_M / 1_000_000 * USD_TO_GBP


def _estimate_tokens(state: dict, questions: dict) -> int:
    state_chars = sum(len(str(v)) for v in state.values())
    question_chars = sum(len(str(q)) for q in questions.values())
    return (state_chars + question_chars) // 4


def _guard(estimated_tokens: int) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Check budget, reserve worst-case cost. Returns (total_spent, reserved).
    Caller must call _release_in_flight(reserved) in a finally block."""
    global _in_flight_cost
    total = spent_gbp()
    worst = _cost_gbp(estimated_tokens)
    if total + _in_flight_cost + worst > BUDGET_GBP:
        raise BudgetExceeded(
            f"LLM budget: £{total:.4f} spent + £{_in_flight_cost:.4f} in-flight, "
            f"this call ~£{worst:.4f}, cap £{BUDGET_GBP:.2f}"
        )
    _in_flight_cost += worst
    return total, worst


def _release_in_flight(reserved: float) -> None:
    global _in_flight_cost
    _in_flight_cost = max(0.0, _in_flight_cost - reserved)


async def _evaluate_async(state: dict, questions: dict) -> tuple[dict, int]:
    item = await evaluate(_get_model(), state, questions)
    input_tokens = item.usage.input_tokens if item.usage else 0
    return item.value, input_tokens


def _safe_json(obj: Any) -> Any:
    if isinstance(obj, (str, int, float, bool)) or obj is None:
        return obj
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        return {k: _safe_json(v) for k, v in obj.items()}
    if isinstance(obj, (list, tuple)):
        return [_safe_json(x) for x in obj]
    try:
        return {k: _safe_json(v) for k, v in vars(obj).items()}
    except TypeError:
        return str(obj)


def _log_call(
    rd: Path,
    started: float,
    total: float,
    purpose: str,
    input_tokens: int,
    state: dict | None = None,
    questions: dict | None = None,
    answers: dict | None = None,
) -> None:
    cost = _cost_gbp(input_tokens)
    latency = round((time.time() - started) * 1000)
    rd.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with _budget_lock:
        with (rd / "llm_calls.jsonl").open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(
                json.dumps(
                    {
                        "ts": round(started, 3),
                        "provider": "jev",
                        "model": _MODEL_ID,
                        "purpose": purpose,
                        "input_tokens": input_tokens,
                        "output_tokens": 0,
                        "cost_gbp": round(cost, 6),
                        "total_gbp": round(total + cost, 6),
                        "latency_ms": latency,
                    }
                )
                + "\n"
            )
        if state is not None or questions is not None or answers is not None:
            with (rd / "llm_prompts.jsonl").open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(
                    json.dumps(
                        {
                            "ts": round(started, 3),
                            "purpose": purpose,
                            "latency_ms": latency,
                            "state": _safe_json(state),
                            "questions": _safe_json(questions),
                            "answers": _safe_json(answers),
                        }
                    )
                    + "\n"
                )


def decide(
    state: dict[str, Any],
    questions: dict[str, NoulQuestion | ChoiceQuestion | ScoreQuestion],
    purpose: str = "",
) -> dict[str, NoulAnswer | ChoiceAnswer | ScoreAnswer]:
    """Ask jev to answer structured questions about `state` (synchronous, sequential).

    answers["key"].noul    — NoulAnswer: probability float [0, 1]
    answers["key"].choice  — ChoiceAnswer: chosen option key string
    answers["key"].score   — ScoreAnswer: float score
    """
    estimated = _estimate_tokens(state, questions)
    with _budget_lock:
        total, reserved = _guard(estimated)

    started = time.time()
    try:
        answers, input_tokens = asyncio.run(_evaluate_async(state, questions))
    finally:
        with _budget_lock:
            _release_in_flight(reserved)

    rd = _run_dir or (_runs_root() / time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S", time.gmtime(started)))
    _log_call(rd, started, total, purpose, input_tokens, state, questions, answers)
    return answers


async def decide_async(
    state: dict[str, Any],
    questions: dict[str, NoulQuestion | ChoiceQuestion | ScoreQuestion],
    purpose: str = "",
) -> dict[str, NoulAnswer | ChoiceAnswer | ScoreAnswer]:
    """Ask jev to answer structured questions about `state` (async, safe for asyncio.gather).

    Must be called from within an active event loop — use asyncio.run() at the top level.
    """
    estimated = _estimate_tokens(state, questions)
    with _budget_lock:
        total, reserved = _guard(estimated)

    started = time.time()
    try:
        answers, input_tokens = await _evaluate_async(state, questions)
    finally:
        with _budget_lock:
            _release_in_flight(reserved)

    rd = _run_dir or (_runs_root() / time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S", time.gmtime(started)))
    _log_call(rd, started, total, purpose, input_tokens, state, questions, answers)
    return answers

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides comprehensive guidance to Claude Code when working with Python code in this repository.

## Core Development Philosophy

### KISS (Keep It Simple, Stupid)

Simplicity should be a key goal in design. Choose straightforward solutions over complex ones whenever possible. Simple solutions are easier to understand, maintain, and debug.

### YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It)

Avoid building functionality on speculation. Implement features only when they are needed, not when you anticipate they might be useful in the future.

### Design Principles

- **Dependency Inversion**: High-level modules should not depend on low-level modules. Both should depend on abstractions.
- **Open/Closed Principle**: Software entities should be open for extension but closed for modification.
- **Single Responsibility**: Each function, class, and module should have one clear purpose.
- **Fail Fast**: Check for potential errors early and raise exceptions immediately when issues occur.

## 🧱 Code Structure & Modularity

### File and Function Limits

- **Never create a file longer than 500 lines of code**. If approaching this limit, refactor by splitting into modules.
- **Functions should be under 50 lines** with a single, clear responsibility.
- **Classes should be under 100 lines** and represent a single concept or entity.
- **Organize code into clearly separated modules**, grouped by feature or responsibility.
- **Line lenght should be max 100 characters** ruff rule in pyproject.toml
- **Use venv_linux** (the virtual environment) whenever executing Python commands, including for unit tests.

### Project Architecture

Follow strict vertical slice architecture with tests living next to the code they test:

```
src/project/
    __init__.py
    main.py
    tests/
        test_main.py
    conftest.py

    # Core modules
    database/
        __init__.py
        connection.py
        models.py
```

"""Row-level observability: every module tags each row, then records one fact per row.

Tag: META_OUTCOME ("pass" / "rejected" / "error") plus META_REJECTION_REASON or META_ERROR_REASON from the
module's own reason sets. Record: sli_observe(rows, MODULE_NAME, start_time, trace_id) ONCE at the end of
main(), on the FULL row list (passed and rejected). Counting is a group-by over runs/<trace_id>/sli_events.jsonl.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import threading
import time

from v2.shared.patterns.worker_runtime import run_dir

META_OUTCOME = "META_OUTCOME"
META_REJECTION_REASON = "META_REJECTION_REASON"
META_ERROR_REASON = "META_ERROR_REASON"

# Serialises concurrent writes from normalization threads (run_in_executor).
# All runs share a single trace_id at a time, so one global lock is sufficient.
_sli_write_lock = threading.Lock()


def passed(rows: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """The rows still tagged "pass"."""
    return [r for r in rows if r.get(META_OUTCOME) == "pass"]


def reject(row: dict, reason: str) -> None:
    """Tag one row as rejected with a reason from the module's REJECTION_REASONS."""
    row[META_OUTCOME] = "rejected"
    row[META_REJECTION_REASON] = reason


def error_out(row: dict, reason: str) -> None:
    """Tag one row as errored with a reason from the module's ERROR_REASONS."""
    row[META_OUTCOME] = "error"
    row[META_ERROR_REASON] = reason


def sli_observe(rows: list[dict], module_name: str, start_time: float, trace_id: str) -> None:
    """One fact per row (never totals) in runs/<trace_id>/sli_events.jsonl."""
    duration_ms = round((time.time() - start_time) * 1000)
    with _sli_write_lock:
        with (run_dir(trace_id) / "sli_events.jsonl").open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for row in rows:
                event = {
                    "META_TRACE_ID": trace_id,
                    "META_WORKER": module_name.split("__")[0],
                    "META_MODULE": module_name,
                    "job_id": row.get("job_id") or row.get("_line"),
                    META_OUTCOME: row.get(META_OUTCOME, "untagged"),
                    META_REJECTION_REASON: row.get(META_REJECTION_REASON),
                    META_ERROR_REASON: row.get(META_ERROR_REASON),
                    "META_DURATION_MS": duration_ms,
                }
                f.write(json.dumps(event) + "\n")

"""The shared worker runtime: the local stand-in for Illumini's streaming runtime.

In production, one SQS message = one user = one trace, and the runtime receives it, validates the context, runs
the handler's STAGE_GRAPH and sends the result on. Here, one profile file = one "message": run_pipeline builds
its context, validates it against the handler's INPUT_CONTEXT_SCHEMA, runs every stage in STAGE_GRAPH order and
validates the result against OUTPUT_CONTEXT_SCHEMA. Handlers, stages and modules never do this plumbing.

    handler.py   HANDLER_NAME + schemas + STAGE_GRAPH of stages        -> run_local_handler / run_pipeline
    stages/*.py  STAGE_NAME + STAGE_GRAPH of modules + inline schemas   -> run_stage_loop
    modules/*.py main(context, prev_data) -> ExecutionResult             (the logic lives here)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import importlib
import json
import os
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from v2.shared.api_calls import llm
from v2.shared.patterns.logging import get_logger, log_event

DEFAULT_JOBS = Path("data/scale_feed.jsonl")
DEFAULT_SEARCH_INPUTS = Path("data/user_search_inputs")
SEARCH_INPUT_FILES = {"companies": "company_searches.json", "titles": "job_title_searches.json",
                      "locations": "location_searches.json"}  # fmt: skip


@dataclass
class ExecutionResult:
    """What every module and stage returns: the rows for the next step, plus named artifacts (e.g. a file path)."""

    trace_id: str
    script_span_id: str
    data: list[dict]
    artifacts: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    metrics: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StageDefinition:
    """One node of a STAGE_GRAPH: a stage (in a handler) or a module (in a stage), by dotted module path."""

    name: str
    module_path: str


def new_trace_id() -> str:
    """Run timestamp, also the run's folder name under runs/."""
    return f"{datetime.now(timezone.utc):%Y%m%dT%H%M%S}"


def run_dir(trace_id: str) -> Path:
    """runs/<trace_id>/ (ILLUMINI_RUNS_DIR overrides runs/), created on first use."""
    path = Path(os.environ.get("ILLUMINI_RUNS_DIR", "runs")) / trace_id
    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return path


def debug_limits() -> tuple[bool, int]:
    """(DEBUG_MODE, DEBUG_LOOPS) from the environment: big loops stop after DEBUG_LOOPS rows in debug mode."""
    return os.environ.get("DEBUG_MODE", "false").lower() == "true", int(os.environ.get("DEBUG_LOOPS", "5"))


def validate_context(context: dict, schema: dict) -> None:
    """Raise ValueError when a non-nullable field is missing or a field has the wrong type."""
    for name, spec in schema["fields"].items():
        value = context.get(name)
        if value is None:
            if not spec["nullable"]:
                raise ValueError(f"context schema {schema['version']}: {name!r} is required")
        elif not isinstance(value, spec["type"]):
            raise ValueError(f"context schema {schema['version']}: {name!r} must be {spec['type'].__name__}")


def run_stage_loop(
    stage_name: str, stage_graph: dict[str, StageDefinition], context: dict, prev_data: list[dict]
) -> ExecutionResult:
    """Run each module in STAGE_GRAPH order, feeding each one the previous module's data."""
    data, artifacts = prev_data, {}
    for node in stage_graph.values():
        result = importlib.import_module(node.module_path).main(context, data)
        data = result.data
        artifacts.update(result.artifacts)
    return ExecutionResult(
        trace_id=context["trace_id"],
        script_span_id=f"{stage_name}_{context['trace_id']}",
        data=data,
        artifacts=artifacts,
        metrics={},
    )


def load_search_inputs(root: Path) -> list[tuple[str, dict]]:
    """(output prefix, profile) per recruiter. Each recruiter is a folder of three search files:
    company_searches.json {"profile_id", "companies"}, job_title_searches.json {"profile_id", "titles"} and
    location_searches.json {"profile_id", "locations"}, read back into one profile. A missing file or a
    profile_id that differs between the three raises. A plain <prefix>.json profile (the older layout) still loads."""
    profiles: list[tuple[str, dict]] = []
    for folder in sorted(p for p in root.iterdir() if p.is_dir()):
        present = {field: folder / name for field, name in SEARCH_INPUT_FILES.items() if (folder / name).exists()}
        if not present:
            continue
        if len(present) != len(SEARCH_INPUT_FILES):
            missing = sorted(set(SEARCH_INPUT_FILES.values()) - {p.name for p in present.values()})
            raise ValueError(f"{folder}: missing search input files {missing}")
        parts = {field: json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) for field, path in present.items()}
        ids = {part["profile_id"] for part in parts.values()}
        if len(ids) != 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{folder}: profile_id differs across the search input files: {sorted(ids)}")
        profiles.append((folder.name, {"profile_id": ids.pop(), **{f: parts[f][f] for f in SEARCH_INPUT_FILES}}))
    for path in sorted(root.glob("*.json")):
        profiles.append((path.stem, json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))))
    return profiles


def run_pipeline(
    stage_graph: dict[str, StageDefinition],
    input_schema: dict,
    output_schema: dict,
    handler_name: str,
    jobs_path: Path,
    search_inputs_dir: Path,
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """One trace per call; one "message" per recruiter in search_inputs_dir. Returns {output file: listed job count}."""
    trace_id = new_trace_id()
    logger = get_logger(handler_name)
    llm.start_run(run_dir(trace_id))
    log_event(logger, "info", "run_started", trace_id, jobs_path=str(jobs_path),
              search_inputs_dir=str(search_inputs_dir))  # fmt: skip
    outputs: dict[str, str] = {}
    for prefix, profile in load_search_inputs(Path(search_inputs_dir)):
        context = {
            "trace_id": trace_id,
            "jobs_path": str(jobs_path),
            "profile": profile,
            "profile_id": profile["profile_id"],
            "output_prefix": prefix,
        }
        validate_context(context, input_schema)
        data: list[dict] = []
        for node in stage_graph.values():
            result = importlib.import_module(node.module_path).main(context, data)
            data = result.data
            context.update(result.artifacts)
        validate_context(context, output_schema)
        outputs[context["output_path"]] = str(len(data))
    log_event(logger, "info", "run_finished", trace_id, outputs=outputs, llm_spent_gbp=round(llm.spent_gbp(), 4))
    return outputs


def run_local_handler(
    stage_graph: dict[str, StageDefinition], input_schema: dict, output_schema: dict, handler_name: str
) -> int:
    """Entry point for `python -m <handler module>`: parse --jobs / --search-inputs, run, print one line per output."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=handler_name)
    parser.add_argument("--jobs", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_JOBS)
    parser.add_argument("--search-inputs", "--briefs", dest="search_inputs", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_SEARCH_INPUTS)
    args, _ = parser.parse_known_args()
    for path, count in run_pipeline(
        stage_graph, input_schema, output_schema, handler_name, args.jobs, args.search_inputs
    ).items():
        print(f"{count:>5} matches -> {path}")
    return 0

1	# Notes
2	
3	## LLM Provider
4	
5	[Vercel AI Gateway](https://vercel.com/ai-gateway/models/jev) is a good fit here — the task is essentially data comparison, so the most important thing is normalizing the data correctly.
6	
7	Links:
8	[habr.com/ru/articles/1085450](https://habr.com/ru/articles/1085450/) Очень крутая статья
9	
10	[habr.com/ru/articles/1087480](https://habr.com/ru/articles/1087480/)
11	
12	[habr.com/ru/articles/1084030](https://habr.com/ru/articles/1084030/)
13	
14	[habr.com/ru/articles/1092000
15	](https://habr.com/ru/articles/1092000/)[habr.com/ru/articles/1089164](https://habr.com/ru/articles/1089164/) Очень крутая статья
16	[habr.com/ru/articles/1086180](https://habr.com/ru/articles/1086180/)
17	
18	---
19	
20	## Architecture
21	
22	### How the runtime builds the recruiter profile
23	
24	`load_search_inputs()` in [worker_runtime.py](v1/shared/patterns/worker_runtime.py) reads the `profile_a/` directory and **merges three files into one dict**:
25	
26	```python
27	{
28	  "profile_id": "a",
29	  "companies":  [{"name": "Aire Calder", "industry": null}, ...],  # from company_searches.json
30	  "titles":     ["Controls Engineer", "Mechanical Engineer", ...],  # from job_title_searches.json
31	  "locations":  [{"name": "Warrington", "type": "sub_region", ...}, ...]  # from location_searches.json
32	}
33	```
34	
35	This dict becomes `context["profile"]` and travels through the entire pipeline.
36	
37	### Job structure in `jobs_raw.jsonl`
38	
39	Each line looks like:
40	
41	```json
42	{
43	  "job_id": "J123456",
44	  "scraped": {
45	    "title":    "Controls Engineer",
46	    "company":  "Aire Calder",
47	    "location": "Warrington",
48	    "salary":   "£45,000"
49	  },
50	  "source_url": "...",
51	  "page": {
52	    "http_status": 200,
53	    "title_tag":   "Controls Engineer | Aire Calder",
54	    "h1":          "Controls Engineer",
55	    "meta":        {},
56	    "visible_text": "...",
57	    "structured_job": {
58	      "title":     "Controls Engineer",
59	      "company":   "Aire Calder",
60	      "locations": ["Warrington"]
61	    }
62	  }
63	}
64	```
65	
66	`scraped.*` — what the scraper extracted from markup (often truncated, empty, or wrong).
67	`page.*` — the raw page fetched once: HTTP status plus all visible fields.
68	
69	### Pipeline flow
70	
71	```
72	jobs_raw.jsonl
73	    │
74	    ▼ load_job_feed
75	    │  → reads line by line; row["page"] and row["scraped"] available
76	    │
77	    ▼ normalise_job_rows
78	    │  → picks only scraped.{title, company, location, salary}
79	    │  → page is kept as-is in row["page"]
80	    │
81	    ▼ drop_duplicate_jobs
82	    │  → dedup by key title|company
83	    │
84	    ▼ resolve_job_town
85	    │  → takes row["location"] from scraped, looks it up in TOWNS dict
86	    │  → adds: row["town"], row["region"], row["country"]
87	    │
88	    ▼ match_jobs   ← profile_a files meet jobs here
89	    │
90	    │  [company check]   row["company"] ∈ {c["name"] for c in profile["companies"]}?
91	    │  [title check]     any t in profile["titles"] is a substring of row["title"]?
92	    │  [location check]  row["town"] ∈ towns_covered(loc) for any loc in profile["locations"]?
93	    │
94	    ▼ portal_matches_output
95	       → writes runs/<trace_id>/profile_a_matched.jsonl
96	```
97	
98	---
99	
100	## Known Bugs in v1
101	
102	### 1. No dead-link filter (critical)
103	
104	The spec says HTTP 404 and 410 must always be rejected. v1 has no such module.
105	
106	| Status    | Count | Note                           |
107	| --------- | ----- | ------------------------------ |
108	| HTTP 200  | 868   | live                           |
109	| HTTP 403  | 455   | blocked (live, scraper failed) |
110	| HTTP 404  | 46    | should be rejected             |
111	| HTTP 410  | 129   | should be rejected             |
112	| HTTP 405  | 3     | live (method not supported)    |
113	| HTTP None | 10    | no page at all                 |
114	
115	8 of 49 "no" labels in `labelled_sample` are 404/410 jobs — they currently pass through to `match_jobs`.
116	
117	---
118	
119	### 2. `resolve_job_town` drops 10 of 11 correct answers
120	
121	Checked all "yes" jobs from `labelled_sample` against the TOWNS dict:
122	
123	| job_id  | scraped.location             | Passes?         |
124	| ------- | ---------------------------- | --------------- |
125	| J685745 | "Runcorn"                    | ✓ only one     |
126	| J849031 | "Birmingham, United Kingdom" | ✗              |
127	| J442509 | "Crewe"                      | ✗ not in TOWNS |
128	| J576140 | "2 Locations"                | ✗              |
129	| J858474 | "Knutsford, Radbroke Hall"   | ✗              |
130	| J355784 | "Bangor Bus Depot"           | ✗              |
131	| J936283 | "Birmingham, United Kingdom" | ✗              |
132	
133	Root causes:
134	
135	- **Country suffix**: `"Birmingham, United Kingdom"` — need to strip `, United Kingdom`
136	- **Unknown cities**: `"Crewe"`, `"Knutsford"` — present in profile `includes`, missing from TOWNS
137	- **Placeholders**: `"2 Locations"`, `"10 Locations"` — must fall back to `structured_job.locations`
138	- **Addresses**: `"Bangor Bus Depot"`, `"Knutsford, Radbroke Hall"` — need city extraction
139	- **Empty location**: 420 jobs have no location — all silently lost
140	
141	---
142	
143	### 3. `scraped.title` contains abbreviations and truncations
144	
145	The scraper frequently stores garbage instead of the real title:
146	
147	| scraped.title | structured_job / title_tag                   |
148	| ------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
149	| "HC engineer" | "HV Commissioning Engineer"                  |
150	| "MD engineer" | "Mechanical Design Engineer"                 |
151	| "SC systems"  | "Software & Control Systems Engineers"       |
152	| "SM manager"  | "Senior Marketing Manager - Financial Lines" |
153	
154	`match_jobs` compares against `row["title"]` which comes from `scraped.title`. The real title is in `page.title_tag` or `page.structured_job.title` — matching must use those.
155	
156	---
157	
158	### 4. `matched_titles` — substring instead of word-by-word matching
159	
160	```python
161	# v1: substring containment
162	return [t for t in titles if t in job_title]
163	```
164	
165	Spec requires: *"every word of the profile title appears in the job's real title in any order, ignoring case, punctuation & a trailing plural s"*.
166	
167	What breaks with substring:
168	
169	- `"cnc miller" in "CNC Miller"` → `False` (case-sensitive)
170	- `"Quality Engineer" in "Quality and Warranty Engineer"` → `False` (words not adjacent)
171	- `"Controls Engineer" in "Senior Controls Engineer"` → `True` — works by coincidence
172	
173	From labelled data: job `J602066` has title `"Quality and Warranty Engineer"` and should match profile title `"Quality Engineer"` (both words present), but substring check returns `False`.
174	
175	---
176	
177	### 5. Company matching — exact equality against `scraped.company` only
178	
179	```python
180	# v1
181	if row["company"] not in companies:  # exact string from scraped.company
182	    reject(row, "COMPANY_NOT_LISTED")
183	```
184	
185	Problems:
186	
187	- `scraped.company` often contains a different company than what's on the page (e.g. `scraped="Viaduct Thornbury Systems"` vs `structured_job.company="Delta North Granary"`)
188	- Profile names include legal suffixes (`Ltd`, `ENGINEERING LTD`, `The Group`, `Holdings`, `UK`) that may differ from scraped data — spec requires fuzzy matching ignoring those suffixes
189	
190	From labelled data: `J809819` — `scraped.company = "Cobalt Zephyr Holdings"`, profile contains `"Cobalt Zephyr"` → should match, but doesn't due to the `Holdings` suffix.
191	
192	Spec also requires checking the company name **across the whole page** (title_tag, h1, URL, visible_text, structured_job) — pipeline only looks at `scraped.company`.
193	
194	---
195	
196	### 6. Remote location type not implemented
197	
198	Profile contains:
199	
200	```json
201	{"name": "Remote (UK)", "type": "remote", "includes": ["Remote", "Home-based", "Work from home"]}
202	```
203	
204	`towns_covered()` returns `{"Remote (UK)", "Remote", "Home-based", "Work from home"}`, but `row["town"]` comes from the TOWNS dict which contains none of these values. Remote jobs never match.
205	
206	Spec: remote = jobs where the employer explicitly states remote/home-based in that country — must check `visible_text` and `structured_job.locations`.
207	
208	---
209	
210	### 7. `structured_job.locations` is never used
211	
212	135 jobs have `structured_job.locations` — a list of strings like `["Birmingham, GB"]`, `["manchester, Lancashire, United Kingdom"]`, `["United Kingdom", "Remote"]`. This is the most reliable location source, but the pipeline ignores it entirely.
213	
214	---
215	
216	### 8. `normalise_job_rows` — silent error swallowing
217	
218	```python
219	try:
220	    scraped = raw["scraped"]
221	    rows.append({...})
222	except Exception:
223	    pass  # row silently lost — no rejection reason, no SLI entry
224	```
225	
226	---
227	
228	### 9. `parse_salary` crashes on real data
229	
230	Values in the feed: `"£50K per Annum"`, `"1K - 3K per Annum"`, `"$2 per Annum"` — all cause `ValueError` inside `int(...)`. Not critical (only 12 jobs have salary), but combined with the `except Exception: pass` above, rows are silently lost.
231	
232	---
233	
234	### 10. Dedup by `title|company` instead of `job_id`
235	
236	[drop_duplicate_jobs.py:18](v1/workers/job_matcher/modules/drop_duplicate_jobs.py#L18): key `f"{row['title']}|{row['company']}"`.
237	
238	Two different jobs at the same company with the same title in different cities will be incorrectly merged. The correct key is `job_id`.
239	
240	## Data Analysis — data/ (excluding golden)
241	
242	### 1. jobs_raw.jsonl — 1,529 jobs
243	
244	HTTP status breakdown:
245	
246	| Status        | Count | %     |
247	| ------------- | ----- | ----- |
248	| 200 OK        | 868   | 56.8% |
249	| 403 Forbidden | 455   | 29.8% |
250	| 410 Gone      | 129   | 8.4%  |
251	| 404 Not Found | 46    | 3.0%  |
252	| Other / empty | 31    | 2.0%  |
253	
254	43% of jobs are inaccessible. Of those, 11.4% are dead links (404/410) that should be filtered.
255	
256	Field fill rates:
257	
258	| Field               | Filled                       |
259	| ------------------- | ---------------------------- |
260	| scraped.title       | 100%                         |
261	| scraped.company     | 100%                         |
262	| scraped.location    | 72.5% (420 missing)          |
263	| scraped.salary      | 0.8% (12 of 1,529)           |
264	| page.title_tag      | 39.8%                        |
265	| page.meta           | 38.8%                        |
266	| page.structured_job | 27.1%                        |
267	| page.h1             | 16.0%                        |
268	| page.visible_text   | 0% (empty in entire dataset) |
269	
270	**Critical finding:** `visible_text` is completely empty across the whole dataset. The company-matching rule from OUTPUT_FORMAT.json (search across page body text) cannot be applied — there is no data to search.
271	
272	### 2. Location signals
273	
274	- Unique location strings: 340
275	- 212 jobs have `"2 Locations"`, 46 have `"3 Locations"`, etc. — these are not parsed
276	- Top real locations: London (37), Derby (32), Bristol (24), Glasgow (17)
277	- Matches against profile cities (naive search): 164 / 1,529 (10.7%)
278	
279	### 3. Title signals (word-level matching)
280	
281	- Unique job titles: 1,348
282	- Matches against profile (all words present in title): 118 / 1,529 (7.7%)
283	- Top matched profile titles: Controls Engineer (24), Electrical Engineer (12), Design Engineer (10), Operations Manager (9), Maintenance Technician (9)
284	
285	### 4. Company signals
286	
287	- Profile companies: 408 (199 with industry specified)
288	- Company matches (normalised): 1,049 / 1,529 (68.6%)
289	- High match rate because the entire feed appears to have been generated from the same company list.
290	
291	### 5. Signal intersection
292	
293	| Condition                              | Jobs          |
294	| -------------------------------------- | ------------- |
295	| Company only                           | 1,049 (68.6%) |
296	| Title only                             | 118 (7.7%)    |
297	| Location only                          | 164 (10.7%)   |

299

301	
302	- yes (match): 11 (18.3%)
303	- no: 49 (81.7%)
304	
305	All 60 job_ids are present in jobs_raw.jsonl. Of the 11 positives, only 9 have `matched_company` / `matched_location` / `matched_job_title` filled; 2 have those fields empty despite `decision=yes` — an annotation anomaly.
306	
307	---
308	
309	## Data investigation: run `20261020T153054` vs `profile_a` inputs
310	
311	### Pipeline funnel — where jobs are lost
312	
313	```
314	load_job_feed        1529  →  pass: 1529 (100%)
315	drop_duplicates      1517  →  pass: 1445 (95.3%)  | rejected: 72 DUPLICATE
316	resolve_job_town     1445  →  pass:     6 (0.4%)  | rejected: 1439 UNKNOWN_LOCATION  ← BOTTLENECK
317	match_jobs              6  →  pass:     2 (33.3%) | rejected: 3 COMPANY_NOT_LISTED, 1 NO_TITLE_MATCH
318	OUTPUT                  2 jobs

322	
323	| Dimension                                           | Matches           | % of 1,529 |

333	### Root cause: `resolve_job_town` only handles bare-city lookup
334	
335	Location format breakdown in the dataset:
336	
337	| Format                           | Count       | Worker handling              |
338	| -------------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------- |
339	| `"City, United Kingdom"`       | 567 (37%)   | ❌ UNKNOWN_LOCATION          |

342	| `"Hybrid - 2 days Warrington"` | 1 (0.1%)    | ❌ UNKNOWN_LOCATION          |

345	Of the 567 jobs with `"City, United Kingdom"` format — **80 have a city from the profile** (Manchester, Birmingham, Liverpool, etc.) and all are lost because the resolver cannot strip the `, United Kingdom` suffix.

349	Only jobs with a **bare city name** (`Wrexham`, `Chester`, `Runcorn`) hit the hardcoded TOWNS dict. Of those:
350	
351	- **2 passed** (Inkwell Copperleaf Group — present in companies list, Wrexham → North Wales)
352	- **3 rejected** at COMPANY_NOT_LISTED (`Mersey Ironbridge`, `Moorside Millrace` — not in the list)

358	
359	- `"Bolton, GB"` — 5 Controls Engineer jobs @ Aire Calder / Aire Northwind / Ancoats Castlefield
360	- `"Manchester, United Kingdom"` — 4 jobs

365	
366	### Conclusion
367	
368	The worker **works** — architecture and contracts are correct. But `resolve_job_town` is an intentionally broken module (noted in CLAUDE.md): it uses exact-match against a tiny hardcoded dict, whereas the real requirement is parsing multi-format location strings. Fixing this module alone would raise output from 2 to ~48 jobs (~24×).
369

372	| Test                                                       | Reason for failure                                                                    |
373	| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
374	| `test_parse_salary_k_suffix`                             | `parse_salary("£50K per Annum")` → `int("50K per Annum")` → `ValueError`     |
375	| `test_parse_salary_range_with_k`                         | `parse_salary("1K - 3K per Annum")` → same error                                   |
