# Notes

## LLM Provider

[Vercel AI Gateway](https://vercel.com/ai-gateway/models/jev) is a good fit here — the task is essentially data comparison, so the most important thing is normalizing the data correctly.

Links:
[habr.com/ru/articles/1085450](https://habr.com/ru/articles/1085450/) Очень крутая статья

[habr.com/ru/articles/1087480](https://habr.com/ru/articles/1087480/)

[habr.com/ru/articles/1084030](https://habr.com/ru/articles/1084030/)

[habr.com/ru/articles/1092000
](https://habr.com/ru/articles/1092000/)[habr.com/ru/articles/1089164](https://habr.com/ru/articles/1089164/) Очень крутая статья
[habr.com/ru/articles/1086180](https://habr.com/ru/articles/1086180/)

---

## Architecture

### How the runtime builds the recruiter profile

`load_search_inputs()` in [worker_runtime.py](v1/shared/patterns/worker_runtime.py) reads the `profile_a/` directory and **merges three files into one dict**:

```python
{
  "profile_id": "a",
  "companies":  [{"name": "Aire Calder", "industry": null}, ...],  # from company_searches.json
  "titles":     ["Controls Engineer", "Mechanical Engineer", ...],  # from job_title_searches.json
  "locations":  [{"name": "Warrington", "type": "sub_region", ...}, ...]  # from location_searches.json
}
```

This dict becomes `context["profile"]` and travels through the entire pipeline.

### Job structure in `jobs_raw.jsonl`

Each line looks like:

```json
{
  "job_id": "J123456",
  "scraped": {
    "title":    "Controls Engineer",
    "company":  "Aire Calder",
    "location": "Warrington",
    "salary":   "£45,000"
  },
  "source_url": "...",
  "page": {
    "http_status": 200,
    "title_tag":   "Controls Engineer | Aire Calder",
    "h1":          "Controls Engineer",
    "meta":        {},
    "visible_text": "...",
    "structured_job": {
      "title":     "Controls Engineer",
      "company":   "Aire Calder",
      "locations": ["Warrington"]
    }
  }
}
```

`scraped.*` — what the scraper extracted from markup (often truncated, empty, or wrong).
`page.*` — the raw page fetched once: HTTP status plus all visible fields.

### Pipeline flow

```
jobs_raw.jsonl
    │
    ▼ load_job_feed
    │  → reads line by line; row["page"] and row["scraped"] available
    │
    ▼ normalise_job_rows
    │  → picks only scraped.{title, company, location, salary}
    │  → page is kept as-is in row["page"]
    │
    ▼ drop_duplicate_jobs
    │  → dedup by key title|company
    │
    ▼ resolve_job_town
    │  → takes row["location"] from scraped, looks it up in TOWNS dict
    │  → adds: row["town"], row["region"], row["country"]
    │
    ▼ match_jobs   ← profile_a files meet jobs here
    │
    │  [company check]   row["company"] ∈ {c["name"] for c in profile["companies"]}?
    │  [title check]     any t in profile["titles"] is a substring of row["title"]?
    │  [location check]  row["town"] ∈ towns_covered(loc) for any loc in profile["locations"]?
    │
    ▼ portal_matches_output
       → writes runs/<trace_id>/profile_a_matched.jsonl
```

---

## Known Bugs in v1

### 1. No dead-link filter (critical)

The spec says HTTP 404 and 410 must always be rejected. v1 has no such module.

| Status    | Count | Note                           |
| --------- | ----- | ------------------------------ |
| HTTP 200  | 868   | live                           |
| HTTP 403  | 455   | blocked (live, scraper failed) |
| HTTP 404  | 46    | should be rejected             |
| HTTP 410  | 129   | should be rejected             |
| HTTP 405  | 3     | live (method not supported)    |
| HTTP None | 10    | no page at all                 |

8 of 49 "no" labels in `labelled_sample` are 404/410 jobs — they currently pass through to `match_jobs`.

---

### 2. `resolve_job_town` drops 10 of 11 correct answers

Checked all "yes" jobs from `labelled_sample` against the TOWNS dict:

| job_id  | scraped.location             | Passes?         |
| ------- | ---------------------------- | --------------- |
| J685745 | "Runcorn"                    | ✓ only one     |
| J849031 | "Birmingham, United Kingdom" | ✗              |
| J442509 | "Crewe"                      | ✗ not in TOWNS |
| J576140 | "2 Locations"                | ✗              |
| J858474 | "Knutsford, Radbroke Hall"   | ✗              |
| J355784 | "Bangor Bus Depot"           | ✗              |
| J936283 | "Birmingham, United Kingdom" | ✗              |

Root causes:

- **Country suffix**: `"Birmingham, United Kingdom"` — need to strip `, United Kingdom`
- **Unknown cities**: `"Crewe"`, `"Knutsford"` — present in profile `includes`, missing from TOWNS
- **Placeholders**: `"2 Locations"`, `"10 Locations"` — must fall back to `structured_job.locations`
- **Addresses**: `"Bangor Bus Depot"`, `"Knutsford, Radbroke Hall"` — need city extraction
- **Empty location**: 420 jobs have no location — all silently lost

---

### 3. `scraped.title` contains abbreviations and truncations

The scraper frequently stores garbage instead of the real title:

| scraped.title | structured_job / title_tag                   |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| "HC engineer" | "HV Commissioning Engineer"                  |
| "MD engineer" | "Mechanical Design Engineer"                 |
| "SC systems"  | "Software & Control Systems Engineers"       |
| "SM manager"  | "Senior Marketing Manager - Financial Lines" |

`match_jobs` compares against `row["title"]` which comes from `scraped.title`. The real title is in `page.title_tag` or `page.structured_job.title` — matching must use those.

---

### 4. `matched_titles` — substring instead of word-by-word matching

```python
# v1: substring containment
return [t for t in titles if t in job_title]
```

Spec requires: *"every word of the profile title appears in the job's real title in any order, ignoring case, punctuation & a trailing plural s"*.

What breaks with substring:

- `"cnc miller" in "CNC Miller"` → `False` (case-sensitive)
- `"Quality Engineer" in "Quality and Warranty Engineer"` → `False` (words not adjacent)
- `"Controls Engineer" in "Senior Controls Engineer"` → `True` — works by coincidence

From labelled data: job `J602066` has title `"Quality and Warranty Engineer"` and should match profile title `"Quality Engineer"` (both words present), but substring check returns `False`.

---

### 5. Company matching — exact equality against `scraped.company` only

```python
# v1
if row["company"] not in companies:  # exact string from scraped.company
    reject(row, "COMPANY_NOT_LISTED")
```

Problems:

- `scraped.company` often contains a different company than what's on the page (e.g. `scraped="Viaduct Thornbury Systems"` vs `structured_job.company="Delta North Granary"`)
- Profile names include legal suffixes (`Ltd`, `ENGINEERING LTD`, `The Group`, `Holdings`, `UK`) that may differ from scraped data — spec requires fuzzy matching ignoring those suffixes

From labelled data: `J809819` — `scraped.company = "Cobalt Zephyr Holdings"`, profile contains `"Cobalt Zephyr"` → should match, but doesn't due to the `Holdings` suffix.

Spec also requires checking the company name **across the whole page** (title_tag, h1, URL, visible_text, structured_job) — pipeline only looks at `scraped.company`.

---

### 6. Remote location type not implemented

Profile contains:

```json
{"name": "Remote (UK)", "type": "remote", "includes": ["Remote", "Home-based", "Work from home"]}
```

`towns_covered()` returns `{"Remote (UK)", "Remote", "Home-based", "Work from home"}`, but `row["town"]` comes from the TOWNS dict which contains none of these values. Remote jobs never match.

Spec: remote = jobs where the employer explicitly states remote/home-based in that country — must check `visible_text` and `structured_job.locations`.

---

### 7. `structured_job.locations` is never used

135 jobs have `structured_job.locations` — a list of strings like `["Birmingham, GB"]`, `["manchester, Lancashire, United Kingdom"]`, `["United Kingdom", "Remote"]`. This is the most reliable location source, but the pipeline ignores it entirely.

---

### 8. `normalise_job_rows` — silent error swallowing

```python
try:
    scraped = raw["scraped"]
    rows.append({...})
except Exception:
    pass  # row silently lost — no rejection reason, no SLI entry
```

---

### 9. `parse_salary` crashes on real data

Values in the feed: `"£50K per Annum"`, `"1K - 3K per Annum"`, `"$2 per Annum"` — all cause `ValueError` inside `int(...)`. Not critical (only 12 jobs have salary), but combined with the `except Exception: pass` above, rows are silently lost.

---

### 10. Dedup by `title|company` instead of `job_id`

[drop_duplicate_jobs.py:18](v1/workers/job_matcher/modules/drop_duplicate_jobs.py#L18): key `f"{row['title']}|{row['company']}"`.

Two different jobs at the same company with the same title in different cities will be incorrectly merged. The correct key is `job_id`.

## Data Analysis — data/ (excluding golden)

### 1. jobs_raw.jsonl — 1,529 jobs

HTTP status breakdown:

| Status        | Count | %     |
| ------------- | ----- | ----- |
| 200 OK        | 868   | 56.8% |
| 403 Forbidden | 455   | 29.8% |
| 410 Gone      | 129   | 8.4%  |
| 404 Not Found | 46    | 3.0%  |
| Other / empty | 31    | 2.0%  |

43% of jobs are inaccessible. Of those, 11.4% are dead links (404/410) that should be filtered.

Field fill rates:

| Field               | Filled                       |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| scraped.title       | 100%                         |
| scraped.company     | 100%                         |
| scraped.location    | 72.5% (420 missing)          |
| scraped.salary      | 0.8% (12 of 1,529)           |
| page.title_tag      | 39.8%                        |
| page.meta           | 38.8%                        |
| page.structured_job | 27.1%                        |
| page.h1             | 16.0%                        |
| page.visible_text   | 0% (empty in entire dataset) |

**Critical finding:** `visible_text` is completely empty across the whole dataset. The company-matching rule from OUTPUT_FORMAT.json (search across page body text) cannot be applied — there is no data to search.

### 2. Location signals

- Unique location strings: 340
- 212 jobs have `"2 Locations"`, 46 have `"3 Locations"`, etc. — these are not parsed
- Top real locations: London (37), Derby (32), Bristol (24), Glasgow (17)
- Matches against profile cities (naive search): 164 / 1,529 (10.7%)

### 3. Title signals (word-level matching)

- Unique job titles: 1,348
- Matches against profile (all words present in title): 118 / 1,529 (7.7%)
- Top matched profile titles: Controls Engineer (24), Electrical Engineer (12), Design Engineer (10), Operations Manager (9), Maintenance Technician (9)

### 4. Company signals

- Profile companies: 408 (199 with industry specified)
- Company matches (normalised): 1,049 / 1,529 (68.6%)
- High match rate because the entire feed appears to have been generated from the same company list.

### 5. Signal intersection

| Condition                              | Jobs          |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Company only                           | 1,049 (68.6%) |
| Title only                             | 118 (7.7%)    |
| Location only                          | 164 (10.7%)   |
| All three (company + title + location) | 35 (2.3%)     |

### 6. labelled_sample.jsonl — 60 labelled jobs

- yes (match): 11 (18.3%)
- no: 49 (81.7%)

All 60 job_ids are present in jobs_raw.jsonl. Of the 11 positives, only 9 have `matched_company` / `matched_location` / `matched_job_title` filled; 2 have those fields empty despite `decision=yes` — an annotation anomaly.

---

## Data investigation: run `20261020T153054` vs `profile_a` inputs

### Pipeline funnel — where jobs are lost

```
load_job_feed        1529  →  pass: 1529 (100%)
drop_duplicates      1517  →  pass: 1445 (95.3%)  | rejected: 72 DUPLICATE
resolve_job_town     1445  →  pass:     6 (0.4%)  | rejected: 1439 UNKNOWN_LOCATION  ← BOTTLENECK
match_jobs              6  →  pass:     2 (33.3%) | rejected: 3 COMPANY_NOT_LISTED, 1 NO_TITLE_MATCH
OUTPUT                  2 jobs
```

### Signal correlation with the dataset

| Dimension                                           | Matches           | % of 1,529 |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ---------- |
| Company (exact match)                               | **1,021**   | 66.8%      |
| Location (token match against towns)                | **136**     | 8.9%       |
| Title (word-match against profile)                  | ~**160**    | ~10.5%     |
| **Triple intersection (manual analysis)**     | **56**      | 3.7%       |
| Of which false-geo (Liverpool NSW, Warrington PA…) | −6               |            |
| **Real UK jobs that should match**            | **~48–50** |            |
| **Worker found**                              | **2**       | 0.13%      |

### Root cause: `resolve_job_town` only handles bare-city lookup

Location format breakdown in the dataset:

| Format                           | Count       | Worker handling              |
| -------------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------- |
| `"City, United Kingdom"`       | 567 (37%)   | ❌ UNKNOWN_LOCATION          |
| Bare city (1–2 words)           | 459 (30%)   | ✅ only if in hardcoded dict |
| Empty string                     | 420 (27.5%) | ❌ UNKNOWN_LOCATION          |
| `"Hybrid - 2 days Warrington"` | 1 (0.1%)    | ❌ UNKNOWN_LOCATION          |
| US/AU false positives            | 15 (1%)     | needs country filter         |

Of the 567 jobs with `"City, United Kingdom"` format — **80 have a city from the profile** (Manchester, Birmingham, Liverpool, etc.) and all are lost because the resolver cannot strip the `, United Kingdom` suffix.

### The 6 jobs that passed the resolver

Only jobs with a **bare city name** (`Wrexham`, `Chester`, `Runcorn`) hit the hardcoded TOWNS dict. Of those:

- **2 passed** (Inkwell Copperleaf Group — present in companies list, Wrexham → North Wales)
- **3 rejected** at COMPANY_NOT_LISTED (`Mersey Ironbridge`, `Moorside Millrace` — not in the list)
- **1 rejected** at NO_TITLE_MATCH (`Software Engineer III, Digital Pathology…` — `systems engineer` is too weak a match)

### Top missed patterns (54 missed of 56)

53 of 54 are blocked at `resolve_job_town`. Main patterns:

- `"Bolton, GB"` — 5 Controls Engineer jobs @ Aire Calder / Aire Northwind / Ancoats Castlefield
- `"Manchester, United Kingdom"` — 4 jobs
- `"Liverpool, United Kingdom"` — 4 jobs
- `"Birmingham, United Kingdom"` — 6 jobs
- `"Knutsford, Radbroke Hall"` — 3 jobs at Lowther Brindley
- `"Wolverhampton, United Kingdom"` — 2 jobs

### Conclusion

The worker **works** — architecture and contracts are correct. But `resolve_job_town` is an intentionally broken module (noted in CLAUDE.md): it uses exact-match against a tiny hardcoded dict, whereas the real requirement is parsing multi-format location strings. Fixing this module alone would raise output from 2 to ~48 jobs (~24×).

## `normalise_job_rows` — 8 tests

| Test                                                       | Reason for failure                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `test_parse_salary_k_suffix`                             | `parse_salary("£50K per Annum")` → `int("50K per Annum")` → `ValueError`     |
| `test_parse_salary_range_with_k`                         | `parse_salary("1K - 3K per Annum")` → same error                                   |
| `test_parse_salary_real_feed_formats[£31K per Annum]`   | K suffix, different amount                                                            |
| `test_parse_salary_real_feed_formats[2 - 3 per Annum]`   | Range without £ or K                                                                 |
| `test_parse_salary_real_feed_formats[15 - 17 per Annum]` | Range without currency symbols                                                        |
| `test_parse_salary_real_feed_formats[$2 per Annum]`      | Dollar sign instead of pound                                                          |
| `test_parse_salary_real_feed_formats[00-14]`             | Hyphenated format with no meaningful value                                            |
| `test_normalise_missing_scraped_has_sli_entry`           | `except Exception: pass` — row is silently lost, nothing is written to the SLI log |

**Root cause:** `parse_salary` does `int(str(value).replace("£","").replace(",",""))` — does not handle suffixes, ranges, or foreign currency symbols.

---

## `drop_duplicate_jobs` — 1 test

| Test                                                          | Reason for failure                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `test_dedup_different_job_ids_same_title_company_both_kept` | Key `title\|company` — two different jobs in different cities with the same title and company are merged into one |

**Root cause:** `dedupe_key` should use `job_id`, not `title|company`.

---

## `resolve_job_town` — 11 tests

| Test                                                                | Reason for failure                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `test_resolve_location_with_country_suffix`                       | `"Birmingham, United Kingdom"` → `lookup_town` performs exact match, suffix not stripped (555 jobs) |
| `test_resolve_location_with_gb_suffix`                            | `"Bolton, GB"` — same, country-code suffix (12 jobs)                                                  |
| `test_resolve_crewe_not_in_towns`                                 | `"Crewe"` — real city, but not in the `TOWNS` dictionary                                            |
| `test_resolve_location_placeholder_fallback`                      | `"2 Locations"` — placeholder, `structured_job.locations` is never checked (337 jobs)               |
| `test_resolve_three_part_location[Derby, Derbyshire, ...]`        | Three-part format: suffix + county not stripped                                                          |
| `test_resolve_three_part_location[Chester, Cheshire, ...]`        | Same                                                                                                     |
| `test_resolve_three_part_location[Bradford, West Yorkshire, ...]` | Same                                                                                                     |
| `test_resolve_three_part_location[Birmingham, Warwickshire, ...]` | Same                                                                                                     |
| `test_resolve_three_part_location[Glasgow, Glasgow City, ...]`    | Same                                                                                                     |
| `test_resolve_hybrid_remote_formats[Hybrid - 2 days Warrington]`  | Embedded city not extracted from hybrid string                                                           |
| `test_resolve_hybrid_remote_formats[Remote - UK]`                 | Remote location type not handled at all                                                                  |

**Root cause:** `lookup_town` only does `TOWNS.get(text.strip().lower())` — a single exact match with no format parsing.

---

## `match_jobs` — 14 tests

| Test                                                                                       | Reason for failure                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `test_matched_titles_case_insensitive`                                                   | `"controls engineer" in "Controls Engineer"` → `False`                           |
| `test_matched_titles_lowercase_profile_title`                                            | `"cnc miller" in "CNC Miller"` → `False`                                         |
| `test_matched_titles_non_adjacent_words`                                                 | `"Quality Engineer" in "Quality and Warranty Engineer"` → `False`                |
| `test_matched_titles_case_real_feed[Business Development Manager]`                       | Profile: `"business development manager"`, feed: `"Business Development Manager"` |
| `test_matched_titles_case_real_feed[Business Development Manager - North]`               | Same + suffix                                                                         |
| `test_matched_titles_case_real_feed[CNC Turner Setter/Programmer ...]`                   | Profile: `"cnc turner"`, feed: `"CNC Turner Setter/..."`                          |
| `test_matched_titles_word_order_real_feed[Engineer - Electrical ...]`                    | Words `"Electrical"` and `"Engineer"` are present but not adjacent                |
| `test_matched_titles_word_order_real_feed[Sr. Applications Engineer - Electrical]`       | Same                                                                                  |
| `test_matched_titles_word_order_real_feed[PSV / HGV Engineer ... / Electrical Engineer]` | Same                                                                                  |
| `test_matched_titles_word_order_real_feed[PSV / HGV Engineer ... / Mechanical Engineer]` | Same                                                                                  |
| `test_matched_titles_word_order_real_feed[Manufacturing Services Technician ...]`        | `"Manufacturing Technician"` — words not adjacent                                  |
| `test_matched_titles_word_order_real_feed[Principal Engineer - Product Safety]`          | `"Product Engineer"` — words not adjacent                                          |
| `test_matched_titles_word_order_real_feed[Highways Engineer – Design ...]`              | `"Design Engineer"` — words not adjacent                                           |
| `test_match_jobs_company_legal_suffix_stripped`                                          | `"Cobalt Zephyr Holdings"` ≠ `"Cobalt Zephyr"` — exact string comparison        |

**Root cause:** `matched_titles` does `t in job_title` — case-sensitive substring, but the spec requires that all words of the profile title appear in the job title in any order.

| Test                                         | Reason for failure                                                                                                                                              |

1	"""Collect location strings and tag remote hints; drop jobs provably outside the profile country."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import re
6	import time
7	
8	from v2.shared.observability.sli_observe import error_out, passed, reject, sli_observe
9	from v2.shared.patterns.logging import get_logger, log_event
10	from v2.shared.patterns.worker_runtime import ExecutionResult
11	
12	MODULE_NAME = "job_matcher__normalise_location"
13	MODULE_TYPE = "filter"
14	REJECTION_REASONS = {"LOCATION_NOT_IN_PROFILE"}
15	ERROR_REASONS = {"PROCESSING_ERROR"}
16	WARNING_REASONS: set[str] = set()
17	
18	_PLACEHOLDER_RE = re.compile(r"^\d+\s+location", re.IGNORECASE)
19	_REMOTE_RE = re.compile(r"\b(remote|home.based|work from home|wfh|home based)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
20	_NON_LATIN_RE = re.compile(r"[　-鿿가-힯Ѐ-ӿ]")  # CJK / Korean / Cyrillic
21	
22	
23	def _collect_location_strings(row: dict) -> list[str]:
24	    """All location text for metadata / downstream use."""
25	    strings: list[str] = []
26	    page = row.get("page") or {}
27	    sj = page.get("structured_job") or {}
28	
29	    for loc in sj.get("locations") or []:
30	        if loc and str(loc).strip():
31	            strings.append(str(loc).strip())
32	
33	    sj_loc = (sj.get("location") or "").strip()
34	    if sj_loc:
35	        strings.append(sj_loc)
36	    for loc in sj.get("additional_locations") or []:
37	        if loc and str(loc).strip():
38	            strings.append(str(loc).strip())
39	
40	    scraped = (row.get("location") or "").strip()
41	    if scraped and not _PLACEHOLDER_RE.match(scraped):
42	        strings.append(scraped)
43	
44	    return strings
45	
46	
47	def _has_non_latin(strings: list[str]) -> bool:
48	    """True if any location string contains non-Latin script (CJK / Korean / Cyrillic).
49	
50	    These are unambiguously non-UK and safe to reject early.  Latin-script
51	    foreign cities (e.g. "Birmingham, AL") are excluded because multinational
52	    companies sometimes declare the wrong city; the agent stage handles those.
53	    """
54	    return any(_NON_LATIN_RE.search(s) for s in strings)
55	
56	
57	logger = get_logger(MODULE_NAME)
58	
59	
60	def main(context: dict, prev_data: list[dict]) -> ExecutionResult:
61	    trace_id = context.get("trace_id")
62	    start_time = time.time()
63	    log_event(logger, "info", "module_start", trace_id, input_count=len(prev_data))
64	
65	    has_remote_profile = any(loc.get("type") == "remote" for loc in context["profile"].get("locations") or [])
66	
67	    for row in prev_data:
68	        try:
69	            strings = _collect_location_strings(row)
70	            row["location_strings"] = strings
71	
72	            is_remote = any(_REMOTE_RE.search(s) for s in strings)
73	            row["is_remote_hint"] = is_remote
74	
75	            if is_remote and has_remote_profile:
76	                continue
77	
78	            if _has_non_latin(strings):
79	                reject(row, "LOCATION_NOT_IN_PROFILE")
80	        except Exception as exc:
81	            log_event(logger, "error", "row_error", trace_id, job_id=row.get("job_id"), error=str(exc))
82	            error_out(row, "PROCESSING_ERROR")
83	
84	    kept = passed(prev_data)
85	    log_event(logger, "info", "module_done", trace_id, kept=len(kept), dropped=len(prev_data) - len(kept))
86	    sli_observe(prev_data, MODULE_NAME, start_time, trace_id)
87	    return ExecutionResult(
88	        trace_id=trace_id,
89	        script_span_id=f"{MODULE_NAME}_{trace_id}",
90	        data=kept,
91	        artifacts={},
92	        metrics={},
93	    )

from tests.v2.conftest import make_row

def test_uk_city_passes(ctx, profile):

    ctx["profile"] = profile
    assert len(main(ctx, [make_row(location="Warrington, United Kingdom")]).data) == 1


def test_uk_city_no_country_suffix_passes(ctx, profile):

def test_non_latin_script_rejected(ctx, profile):

# PRP: v2 Job Matcher — Complete Implementation

## Goal

Implement a production-quality v2 job matcher that:

1. Normalization = soft pre-filter using profile data (not hardcoded dicts)
2. Implements the full matching agent (company + title + location + LLM batch for location)
3. Processes 200 000 jobs in < 20 minutes via configurable chunked parallel workers
4. Uses Jev (Vercel AI Gateway) as the LLM provider — calls are parallel across chunks
5. Generates a markdown summary report at the end of each run

The output of a successful run is:
- `runs/<trace_id>/profile_a_matched.jsonl` — one JSON line per matched job
- `runs/<trace_id>/report.md` — pipeline statistics + matched job list

---

## Why

- v1 matches **0 of 11** labelled YES jobs — all lost at `resolve_job_town` (tiny hardcoded dict, exact match only).
- v2 stubs are pass-through only — no normalization, no matching, no parallelism.
- The private test dataset expects ≥ 90 % agreement with production; v1 gets 0 %.
- The task requires 200 000 jobs in 20 minutes; the current single-threaded pipeline cannot scale.

---

## What

### Matching rules (from `OUTPUT_FORMAT.json` — do NOT relax these)

| Signal | Rule |
|--------|------|
| **Company** | Fuzzy: ignore case/punctuation/leading "The"/legal suffixes (Ltd, plc, Group, Holdings, International, UK, Limited, Engineering, Services, Solutions, Systems, Technologies, Co). |
| **Title** | Every word of the profile title appears in the job's resolved title in any order, ignoring case, punctuation, trailing plural *s*. One job can match multiple profile titles. |
| **Location** | A `city` covers its own name + `includes`. A `sub_region` covers its name + `includes`. `remote` covers jobs the employer explicitly marks remote/home-based in that country. Multiple job locations: pass if **any** matches. Jobs in a different country never match. |
| **Live** | HTTP 404 or 410 → rejected unconditionally. |
| **Output** | `matched_job_title` and `matched_location` list **every** profile entry that matched, spelled exactly as in the profile. |

### Architecture overview

```
handler.py
  │
  ├─ load_job_feed (serial, I/O)
  │    └─ all 200k rows in memory
  │
  ├─ split into N chunks  (CHUNK_SIZE env var, default 1000)
  │
  └─ ThreadPoolExecutor (LLM calls are network I/O → real parallelism, GIL releases)
       │
       ├─ chunk_1 ──► stage_normalise ──► pre_filter ──► LLM batch ──► exact_match ─┐
       ├─ chunk_2 ──► stage_normalise ──► pre_filter ──► LLM batch ──► exact_match  ├─► merge
       └─ chunk_N ──► stage_normalise ──► pre_filter ──► LLM batch ──► exact_match ─┘
                                                              ▲
                                              threading.Lock only on budget file read/write
                                              (not on the API call itself → true parallelism)
       │
       ├─ stage_output  (serial, I/O)
       └─ stage_report  (serial)
```

### Normalization = soft pre-filter

Each normalization module has **two responsibilities**:
1. Extract the best available signal (priority chain across page fields)
2. Soft pre-filter: reject rows where NO token from ANY source even *could* match the profile

The profile itself is the reference — no hardcoded city/company dictionaries.

```
resolve_company:  build profile_company_tokens from profile["companies"]
                  reject if resolved_company shares no token with profile_company_tokens
                  → rejects ~30% irrelevant jobs early

resolve_title:    build profile_title_words from profile["titles"]
                  reject if resolved_title shares no word with profile_title_words
                  → rejects ~40% more

resolve_location: build profile_city_set from all profile["locations"][*].includes

content.thinking:
Now I have a very thorough understanding of the codebase. Let me analyze the problems and devise the PRP:

## Problems in the current `match_jobs.py` implementation:

### 1. `rejection_reason` is computed in parallel with match questions (BIG BUG)
The current code asks `rejection_reason` as a ChoiceQuestion alongside company/title/location questions in one batch. The model doesn't know the outcomes of the other questions — it can only see the raw state. So it guesses, and guesses wrong (DEAD_LINK=0.36 when it should be WRONG_COUNTRY=0.01).
The fix is to drop rejection_reason from the question batch and instead derive it deterministically afterward in Python: check the company score against threshold first, then check if any title matched, then fall through to a location check using the resolved answers.

Still writing rejection logic...

I'm noticing another inefficiency: 57 title questions get sent per job even though only one or two ever score above threshold. I should add deterministic pre-filtering in Python that checks for word overlap between job title and candidate titles before bothering to ask the full matching system, cutting out the obvious non-matches first.

Looking at the log example, a title like "Controls Engineer" triggers 57 Jev title questions even though only one actually matches well — the rest score near zero. The fix is to deterministically pre-filter before calling Jev: skip questions where title words have zero overlap with the job title, and skip location questions entirely when all location strings are empty, setting those scores to 0.0 without an API call. This cuts token usage and latency significantly.

Another angle is prompt caching for the company list, since the same ~300 companies are listed for every job and only the state (title, location, company name) varies. Jev's SDK doesn't expose explicit caching controls, but if questions are built once per run and passed by reference in a stable order, Anthropic's automatic prompt caching might already apply — though without seeing jev's internals, I'd need to verify this by checking token counts across calls.

"""v2 job matcher handler — parallel chunked pipeline."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import importlib
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from v2.shared.api_calls import llm
from v2.shared.patterns.logging import configure_file_logging, get_logger, log_event
from v2.shared.patterns.worker_runtime import (
    DEFAULT_JOBS,
    DEFAULT_SEARCH_INPUTS,
    load_search_inputs,
    new_trace_id,
    run_dir,
    validate_context,
)
from v2.shared.schemas.job_matcher.v1 import JOB_MATCHER_SCHEMA as OUTPUT_CONTEXT_SCHEMA
from v2.shared.schemas.pipeline_start_takehome.v1 import PIPELINE_START_TAKEHOME_SCHEMA as INPUT_CONTEXT_SCHEMA

HANDLER_NAME = "job_matcher"
VERSION = "v2.0.0"


def run_parallel_pipeline(jobs_path: Path, search_inputs_dir: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Load all jobs once, run parallel normalization+agent per recruiter, then output."""
    trace_id = new_trace_id()
    logger = get_logger(HANDLER_NAME)
    rd = run_dir(trace_id)
    llm.start_run(rd)
    configure_file_logging(rd)
    log_event(logger, "info", "run_started", trace_id, jobs_path=str(jobs_path))

    stage_clean_jobs = importlib.import_module("v2.workers.job_matcher.stages.stage_clean_jobs")
    stage_output = importlib.import_module("v2.workers.job_matcher.stages.stage_output")
    stage_report = importlib.import_module("v2.workers.job_matcher.stages.stage_report")
    chunk_runner = importlib.import_module("v2.workers.job_matcher.chunk_runner")

    outputs: dict[str, str] = {}
    for prefix, profile in load_search_inputs(Path(search_inputs_dir)):
        context = {
            "trace_id": trace_id,
            "jobs_path": str(jobs_path),
            "profile": profile,
            "profile_id": profile["profile_id"],
            "output_prefix": prefix,
        }
        validate_context(context, INPUT_CONTEXT_SCHEMA)

        # Stage 1: load
        load_result = stage_clean_jobs.main(context, [])
        all_rows = load_result.data

        # Stages 2+3: normalize + agent in parallel chunks
        matched = chunk_runner.run_chunks(all_rows, context)

        # Stage 4: output
        output_result = stage_output.main(context, matched)
        context.update(output_result.artifacts)

        validate_context(context, OUTPUT_CONTEXT_SCHEMA)
        outputs[context["output_path"]] = str(len(output_result.data))

    # Stage 5: report (per run, after all profiles)
    report_context = {"trace_id": trace_id, "runs_dir": str(rd)}
    stage_report.main(report_context, [])

    log_event(logger, "info", "run_finished", trace_id, outputs=outputs,
              llm_spent_gbp=round(llm.spent_gbp(), 4))  # fmt: skip
    return outputs


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=HANDLER_NAME)
    parser.add_argument("--jobs", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_JOBS)
    parser.add_argument("--search-inputs", "--briefs", dest="search_inputs",
                        type=Path, default=DEFAULT_SEARCH_INPUTS)  # fmt: skip
    args, _ = parser.parse_known_args()
    for path, count in run_parallel_pipeline(args.jobs, args.search_inputs).items():
        print(f"{count:>5} matches -> {path}")
    sys.exit(0)

"""Resolve company name from page signals; soft-filter obviously non-matching companies."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import time

from v2.shared.observability.sli_observe import error_out, passed, reject, sli_observe
from v2.shared.patterns.logging import get_logger, log_event
from v2.shared.patterns.worker_runtime import ExecutionResult

MODULE_NAME = "job_matcher__resolve_company"
MODULE_TYPE = "filter"
REJECTION_REASONS = {"COMPANY_NOT_IN_PROFILE"}
ERROR_REASONS = {"PROCESSING_ERROR"}
WARNING_REASONS: set[str] = set()

_LEGAL_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(ltd|limited|plc|group|holdings|international|uk|engineering|services|"
    r"solutions|systems|technologies|technology|co|inc|corp|corporation|gmbh|llc|"
    r"company|industries|manufacturing|the|global|europe|consulting|consultancy|"
    r"partners|recruitment|staffing|personnel|associates|agency|firm)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
_PUNCT_RE = re.compile(r"[^\w\s]")
_SPACE_RE = re.compile(r"\s+")


def _tokenize(name: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    s = name.lower()
    s = _LEGAL_RE.sub(" ", s)
    s = _PUNCT_RE.sub(" ", s)
    s = _SPACE_RE.sub(" ", s).strip()
    return frozenset(w for w in s.split() if len(w) > 1)


def _resolve_company_name(row: dict) -> str:
    page = row.get("page") or {}
    sj = page.get("structured_job") or {}
    structured = (sj.get("company") or "").strip()
    if structured:
        return structured
    return row.get("company", "").strip()


def _build_profile_company_tokensets(companies: list) -> list[frozenset[str]]:
    result = []
    for c in companies:
        name = c.get("name", "") if isinstance(c, dict) else str(c)
        toks = _tokenize(name)
        if toks:
            result.append(toks)
    return result


logger = get_logger(MODULE_NAME)


def main(context: dict, prev_data: list[dict]) -> ExecutionResult:
    trace_id: str = context.get("trace_id") or ""
    start_time = time.time()
    log_event(logger, "info", "module_start", trace_id, input_count=len(prev_data))

    profile_tokensets = _build_profile_company_tokensets(context["profile"].get("companies") or [])

    for row in prev_data:
        try:
            resolved = _resolve_company_name(row)
            row["resolved_company"] = resolved
            job_toks = _tokenize(resolved)
            if not any(ct <= job_toks for ct in profile_tokensets):
                reject(row, "COMPANY_NOT_IN_PROFILE")
        except Exception as exc:
            log_event(logger, "error", "row_error", trace_id, job_id=row.get("job_id"), error=str(exc))
            error_out(row, "PROCESSING_ERROR")

    kept = passed(prev_data)
    log_event(logger, "info", "module_done", trace_id, kept=len(kept), dropped=len(prev_data) - len(kept))
    sli_observe(prev_data, MODULE_NAME, start_time, trace_id)
    return ExecutionResult(
        trace_id=trace_id,
        script_span_id=f"{MODULE_NAME}_{trace_id}",
        data=kept,
        artifacts={},
        metrics={},
    )

# PRP: Improve match_jobs Jev Prompt Quality

## Goal

Fix four concrete defects in `v2/workers/job_matcher/agent/match_jobs.py` that
cause incorrect rejection reasons, wasted tokens, and avoidable model confusion.
Only this one file and a new test file change.

## Why

- **Wrong rejection reason logged**: for a US job (Warrington, PA) the recorded
  reason is `DEAD_LINK` (0.36 confidence) instead of `WRONG_COUNTRY`.  Root cause:
  `rejection_reason` is asked as a ChoiceQuestion in parallel with match questions.
  The model never sees whether company=0.99, title=0.98, locs≈0 — it only sees raw
  state and guesses.
- **Token waste on obvious non-matches**: all 57 profile titles are sent for every
  job, though at most 1–3 are plausible.  For "Controls Engineer", 56 of 57 title
  questions return 0.02–0.03 — pure waste.
- **300-line company list on every call**: the company NoulQuestion embeds the full
  list of ~300 companies.  `_find_matched_company()` (already in the file) can find
  the single best candidate before the call, reducing the company instruction from
  ~5 000 chars to ~100 chars.
- **No country signal in state**: when `location_strings` = `["Warrington, PA,
  United States"]`, loc questions for UK regions (Runcorn, Warrington UK) return
  0.03–0.07 instead of 0.0 because the model sees "Warrington" in both the state
  and the includes lists.  Explicitly adding `"location_country"` to the state
  gives the model an unambiguous signal.

## What

Single file edit: `v2/workers/job_matcher/agent/match_jobs.py`
New test file:   `tests/v2/test_match_jobs.py`

### Concrete changes inside `match_jobs.py`

| Change | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| rejection_reason | ChoiceQuestion sent to jev | Removed from questions; computed deterministically in Python after answers received |
| title questions | 57 NoulQuestion per call | Only titles with ≥1 overlapping word with resolved_title |
| company question | 300-line list in instructions | Pre-find candidate with `_find_matched_company`; ask jev to confirm only that candidate; if no candidate → reject immediately |
| state | missing country signal | Add `"location_country"` derived from `_detect_location_country(location_strings)` |

### Success Criteria

- [ ] `rejection_reason` for Warrington PA job → `WRONG_COUNTRY`, not `DEAD_LINK`
- [ ] Title questions per call ≤ (number of titles sharing words with job title)
- [ ] Company instruction length < 200 chars (single company name, not full list)
- [ ] State includes `"location_country"` key
- [ ] All existing tests pass: `pytest tests/ -q`
- [ ] New unit tests pass: `pytest tests/v2/test_match_jobs.py -v`

---

## All Needed Context

### Files to Read Before Coding

```yaml
- file: v2/workers/job_matcher/agent/match_jobs.py
  why: The only file being modified; know every function

- file: v2/shared/api_calls/llm.py
  why: decide_async() signature; NoulQuestion / ChoiceQuestion dataclasses

- file: v2/workers/job_matcher/normalization/resolve_company.py
  why: _tokenize() and _find_matched_company() are mirrors of the same logic here;
       by the time rows reach match_jobs, resolved_company already passed token-overlap
       check — so _find_matched_company will always return a candidate (or reject)

- file: v2/workers/job_matcher/normalization/resolve_title.py
  why: _title_words() does the same de-pluralising / splitting as what we need
       to pre-filter title questions

- file: v2/shared/observability/sli_observe.py
  why: passed() / reject() / sli_observe() contract

- file: tests/v2/conftest.py
  why: make_row() helper; ctx/profile fixtures; copy the pattern exactly

- file: tests/v2/normalizations/conftest.py
  why: fresh_rows(), golden fixtures (gctx, golden_rows, yes_ids)

- file: tests/v2/normalizations/test_normalise_location.py
  why: exact test file structure to mirror for test_match_jobs.py
```

### Real logged call to understand the problem

The JSON below is from `runs/20261023T185439/llm_prompts.jsonl` — a real failure case:

```
state: company="Aire Calder", title="Controls Engineer",
       location_strings=["Warrington, PA, United States", "Warrington, PA, United States"],
       is_remote=false
answers:
  company = 0.99   ← passes
  title_10 = 0.98  ← "Controls Engineer" passes
  all title_* except title_10 ≈ 0.02
  loc_6 = 0.04 (M62 Corridor), loc_7 = 0.07 (Runcorn), loc_8 = 0.03 (Warrington UK)
  all locs < 0.50  ← fails
  rejection_reason.choice = "DEAD_LINK"  (confidence 0.23!)
    probabilities: WRONG_COMPANY=0.35, WRONG_TITLE=0.06, WRONG_LOCATION=0.18,
                   WRONG_COUNTRY=0.01, DEAD_LINK=0.36, MULTI_FAIL=0.04
```

The correct answer is `WRONG_COUNTRY`.  The model guessed `DEAD_LINK` because it
cannot see that company=0.99 and title=0.98 already passed.  Confidence 0.23 proves
the model is uncertain — it's guessing.

### Codebase Conventions (must follow)

```python

MODULE_NAME = "job_matcher__match_jobs"

### Change 1 — Remove rejection_reason ChoiceQuestion; add `_derive_rejection_reason`

```python
# REMOVE from _build_questions():
questions["rejection_reason"] = ChoiceQuestion(...)   # DELETE

# ADD new helpers above _build_questions():

_OUTSIDE_UK_MARKERS = (
    "united states", "united states of america", "canada", "australia",
    "new zealand", " pa,", " tx,", " ny,", " ca,", " fl,", " va,",
    " al ", " al,",  # US state abbreviations in "city, ST," format
)

def _detect_location_country(location_strings: list[str]) -> str:
    """Return 'United States', 'United Kingdom', or '' (unknown).

    Only fires on unambiguous signals (country names or US state codes).
    Latin-script foreign cities without country suffix → return '' so the
    agent stage can decide.
    """
    lower_strings = [s.lower() for s in location_strings]
    for s in lower_strings:
        if any(m in s for m in _OUTSIDE_UK_MARKERS):
            return "United States"  # simplified; extend if needed
    for s in lower_strings:
        if "united kingdom" in s or " uk" in s or ", gb" in s:
            return "United Kingdom"
    return ""


def _derive_rejection_reason(
    answers: dict,
    asked_title_indices: list[int],
    n_locs: int,
    location_strings: list[str],
) -> str:
    """Deterministic rejection reason; called only when the row is being rejected."""
    company_ans = answers.get("company")
    if not company_ans or company_ans.noul <= _MATCH_THRESHOLD:
        return "WRONG_COMPANY"

    has_title = any(
        (a := answers.get(f"title_{i}")) and a.noul > _MATCH_THRESHOLD
        for i in asked_title_indices
    )
    if not has_title:
        return "WRONG_TITLE"

    # Company + title passed; location failed
    country = _detect_location_country(location_strings)
    if country and country != "United Kingdom":
        return "WRONG_COUNTRY"
    return "WRONG_LOCATION"

### Change 2 — Add `location_country` to state

```python

### Change 3 — Company pre-filter + single-candidate question

### Change 4 — Pre-filter title questions

```python
# ADD helper:

_TITLE_SPLIT_RE = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9\s]")

def _title_word_set(text: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    words = _TITLE_SPLIT_RE.sub(" ", text.lower()).split()
    return frozenset(w.rstrip("s") for w in words if len(w) > 2)

def _relevant_title_indices(job_title: str, titles: list[str]) -> list[int]:
    """Indices of profile titles that share ≥1 word with the job title."""
    job_words = _title_word_set(job_title)
    return [
        i for i, t in enumerate(titles)
        if _title_word_set(t) & job_words
    ]

# In _process_row(), BEFORE the jev call:
asked_title_indices = _relevant_title_indices(state["title"], titles)
# Build per-row questions (remove all title_* from base, add only relevant ones)
row_questions = {k: v for k, v in row_questions.items() if not k.startswith("title_")}
for i in asked_title_indices:
    row_questions[f"title_{i}"] = questions[f"title_{i}"]
```

Replace the existing `rejection_reason = _get_rejection_reason(answers)` pattern:

if not company_ans or company_ans.noul <= _MATCH_THRESHOLD:

]

matched_locs = [

]

row["matched_company"]   = candidate_company   # ← use pre-computed value

## Goal

Fix four concrete defects in `v2/workers/job_matcher/agent/match_jobs.py` that
cause incorrect rejection reasons, wasted tokens, and avoidable model confusion.
Only this one file and a new test file change.

## Why

- **Wrong rejection reason logged**: for a US job (Warrington, PA) the recorded
  reason is `DEAD_LINK` (0.36 confidence) instead of `WRONG_COUNTRY`.  Root cause:
  `rejection_reason` is asked as a ChoiceQuestion in parallel with match questions.
  The model never sees whether company=0.99, title=0.98, locs≈0 — it only sees raw
  state and guesses.
- **Token waste on obvious non-matches**: all 57 profile titles are sent for every
  job, though at most 1–3 are plausible.  For "Controls Engineer", 56 of 57 title
  questions return 0.02–0.03 — pure waste.
- **300-line company list on every call**: the company NoulQuestion embeds the full
  list of ~300 companies.  `_find_matched_company()` (already in the file) can find
  the single best candidate before the call, reducing the company instruction from
  ~5 000 chars to ~100 chars.
- **No country signal in state**: when `location_strings` = `["Warrington, PA,
  United States"]`, loc questions for UK regions (Runcorn, Warrington UK) return
  0.03–0.07 instead of 0.0 because the model sees "Warrington" in both the state
  and the includes lists.  Explicitly adding `"location_country"` to the state
  gives the model an unambiguous signal.

## Implementation Blueprint

### Change 1 — Remove rejection_reason ChoiceQuestion; add `_derive_rejection_reason`

```python
# REMOVE from _build_questions():
questions["rejection_reason"] = ChoiceQuestion(...)   # DELETE

# ADD new helpers above _build_questions():

_OUTSIDE_UK_MARKERS = (
    "united states", "united states of america", "canada", "australia",
    "new zealand", " pa,", " tx,", " ny,", " ca,", " fl,", " va,",
    " al ", " al,",  # US state abbreviations in "city, ST," format
)

def _detect_location_country(location_strings: list[str]) -> str:
    """Return 'United States', 'United Kingdom', or '' (unknown).

    Only fires on unambiguous signals (country names or US state codes).
    Latin-script foreign cities without country suffix → return '' so the
    agent stage can decide.
    """
    lower_strings = [s.lower() for s in location_strings]
    for s in lower_strings:
        if any(m in s for m in _OUTSIDE_UK_MARKERS):
            return "United States"  # simplified; extend if needed
    for s in lower_strings:
        if "united kingdom" in s or " uk" in s or ", gb" in s:
            return "United Kingdom"
    return ""


def _derive_rejection_reason(
    answers: dict,
    asked_title_indices: list[int],
    n_locs: int,
    location_strings: list[str],
) -> str:
    """Deterministic rejection reason; called only when the row is being rejected."""
    company_ans = answers.get("company")
    if not company_ans or company_ans.noul <= _MATCH_THRESHOLD:
        return "WRONG_COMPANY"

    has_title = any(
        (a := answers.get(f"title_{i}")) and a.noul > _MATCH_THRESHOLD
        for i in asked_title_indices
    )
    if not has_title:
        return "WRONG_TITLE"

    # Company + title passed; location failed
    country = _detect_location_country(location_strings)
    if country and country != "United Kingdom":
        return "WRONG_COUNTRY"
    return "WRONG_LOCATION"
```

# ADD helper:

_TITLE_SPLIT_RE = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9\s]")

def _title_word_set(text: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    words = _TITLE_SPLIT_RE.sub(" ", text.lower()).split()
    return frozenset(w.rstrip("s") for w in words if len(w) > 2)

def _relevant_title_indices(job_title: str, titles: list[str]) -> list[int]:
    """Indices of profile titles that share ≥1 word with the job title."""
    job_words = _title_word_set(job_title)
    return [
        i for i, t in enumerate(titles)
        if _title_word_set(t) & job_words
    ]

# In _process_row(), BEFORE the jev call:
asked_title_indices = _relevant_title_indices(state["title"], titles)
# Build per-row questions (remove all title_* from base, add only relevant ones)
row_questions = {k: v for k, v in row_questions.items() if not k.startswith("title_")}
for i in asked_title_indices:
    row_questions[f"title_{i}"] = questions[f"title_{i}"]

133	```python

135	questions["rejection_reason"] = ChoiceQuestion(...)   # DELETE
136	
137	# ADD new helpers above _build_questions():
138	
139	_OUTSIDE_UK_MARKERS = (
140	    "united states", "united states of america", "canada", "australia",
141	    "new zealand", " pa,", " tx,", " ny,", " ca,", " fl,", " va,",
142	    " al ", " al,",  # US state abbreviations in "city, ST," format
143	)

145	def _detect_location_country(location_strings: list[str]) -> str:
146	    """Return 'United States', 'United Kingdom', or '' (unknown).
147	
148	    Only fires on unambiguous signals (country names or US state codes).
149	    Latin-script foreign cities without country suffix → return '' so the
150	    agent stage can decide.
151	    """
152	    lower_strings = [s.lower() for s in location_strings]
153	    for s in lower_strings:
154	        if any(m in s for m in _OUTSIDE_UK_MARKERS):
155	            return "United States"  # simplified; extend if needed
156	    for s in lower_strings:
157	        if "united kingdom" in s or " uk" in s or ", gb" in s:
158	            return "United Kingdom"
159	    return ""
160	
161	
162	def _derive_rejection_reason(
163	    answers: dict,
164	    asked_title_indices: list[int],
165	    n_locs: int,
166	    location_strings: list[str],
167	) -> str:
168	    """Deterministic rejection reason; called only when the row is being rejected."""
169	    company_ans = answers.get("company")
170	    if not company_ans or company_ans.noul <= _MATCH_THRESHOLD:
171	        return "WRONG_COMPANY"
172	
173	    has_title = any(
174	        (a := answers.get(f"title_{i}")) and a.noul > _MATCH_THRESHOLD
175	        for i in asked_title_indices
176	    )
177	    if not has_title:
178	        return "WRONG_TITLE"
179	
180	    # Company + title passed; location failed
181	    country = _detect_location_country(location_strings)
182	    if country and country != "United Kingdom":
183	        return "WRONG_COUNTRY"
184	    return "WRONG_LOCATION"

# PRP: Improve match_jobs Jev Prompt Quality

## Goal

Fix four concrete defects in `v2/workers/job_matcher/agent/match_jobs.py` that
cause incorrect rejection reasons, wasted tokens, and avoidable model confusion.
Only this one file and a new test file change.

## Why

- **Wrong rejection reason logged**: for a US job (Warrington, PA) the recorded
  reason is `DEAD_LINK` (0.36 confidence) instead of `WRONG_COUNTRY`.  Root cause:
  `rejection_reason` is asked as a ChoiceQuestion in parallel with match questions.
  The model never sees whether company=0.99, title=0.98, locs≈0 — it only sees raw
  state and guesses.
- **Token waste on obvious non-matches**: all 57 profile titles are sent for every
  job, though at most 1–3 are plausible.  For "Controls Engineer", 56 of 57 title
  questions return 0.02–0.03 — pure waste.
- **300-line company list on every call**: the company NoulQuestion embeds the full
  list of ~300 companies.  `_find_matched_company()` (already in the file) can find
  the single best candidate before the call, reducing the company instruction from
  ~5 000 chars to ~100 chars.
- **No country signal in state**: when `location_strings` = `["Warrington, PA, United States"]`, loc questions for UK regions (Runcorn, Warrington UK) return
  0.03–0.07 instead of 0.0 because the model sees "Warrington" in both the state
  and the includes lists.  Explicitly adding `"location_country"` to the state
  gives the model an unambiguous signal.

## What

Single file edit: `v2/workers/job_matcher/agent/match_jobs.py`
New test file:   `tests/v2/test_match_jobs.py`

### Concrete changes inside `match_jobs.py`

| Change           | Before                        | After                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| rejection_reason | ChoiceQuestion sent to jev    | Removed from questions; computed deterministically in Python after answers received                                              |
| title questions  | 57 NoulQuestion per call      | Only titles with ≥1 overlapping word with resolved_title                                                                        |
| company question | 300-line list in instructions | Pre-find candidate with `_find_matched_company`; ask jev to confirm only that candidate; if no candidate → reject immediately |
| state            | missing country signal        | Add `"location_country"` derived from `_detect_location_country(location_strings)`                                           |

### Success Criteria

- [ ] `rejection_reason` for Warrington PA job → `WRONG_COUNTRY`, not `DEAD_LINK`
- [ ] Title questions per call ≤ (number of titles sharing words with job title)
- [ ] Company instruction length < 200 chars (single company name, not full list)
- [ ] State includes `"location_country"` key
- [ ] All existing tests pass: `pytest tests/ -q`
- [ ] New unit tests pass: `pytest tests/v2/test_match_jobs.py -v`

---

## All Needed Context

### Files to Read Before Coding

```yaml
- file: v2/workers/job_matcher/agent/match_jobs.py
  why: The only file being modified; know every function

- file: v2/shared/api_calls/llm.py
  why: decide_async() signature; NoulQuestion / ChoiceQuestion dataclasses

- file: v2/workers/job_matcher/normalization/resolve_company.py
  why: _tokenize() and _find_matched_company() are mirrors of the same logic here;
       by the time rows reach match_jobs, resolved_company already passed token-overlap
       check — so _find_matched_company will always return a candidate (or reject)

- file: v2/workers/job_matcher/normalization/resolve_title.py
  why: _title_words() does the same de-pluralising / splitting as what we need
       to pre-filter title questions

- file: v2/shared/observability/sli_observe.py
  why: passed() / reject() / sli_observe() contract

- file: tests/v2/conftest.py
  why: make_row() helper; ctx/profile fixtures; copy the pattern exactly

- file: tests/v2/normalizations/conftest.py
  why: fresh_rows(), golden fixtures (gctx, golden_rows, yes_ids)

- file: tests/v2/normalizations/test_normalise_location.py
  why: exact test file structure to mirror for test_match_jobs.py
```

### Real logged call to understand the problem

The JSON below is from `runs/20261023T185439/llm_prompts.jsonl` — a real failure case:

```
state: company="Aire Calder", title="Controls Engineer",
       location_strings=["Warrington, PA, United States", "Warrington, PA, United States"],
       is_remote=false
answers:
  company = 0.99   ← passes
  title_10 = 0.98  ← "Controls Engineer" passes
  all title_* except title_10 ≈ 0.02
  loc_6 = 0.04 (M62 Corridor), loc_7 = 0.07 (Runcorn), loc_8 = 0.03 (Warrington UK)
  all locs < 0.50  ← fails
  rejection_reason.choice = "DEAD_LINK"  (confidence 0.23!)
    probabilities: WRONG_COMPANY=0.35, WRONG_TITLE=0.06, WRONG_LOCATION=0.18,
                   WRONG_COUNTRY=0.01, DEAD_LINK=0.36, MULTI_FAIL=0.04
```

The correct answer is `WRONG_COUNTRY`.  The model guessed `DEAD_LINK` because it
cannot see that company=0.99 and title=0.98 already passed.  Confidence 0.23 proves
the model is uncertain — it's guessing.

### Codebase Conventions (must follow)

```python
# Module-level constants expected by the runtime
MODULE_NAME = "job_matcher__match_jobs"
MODULE_TYPE = "filter"  # not "transform"
REJECTION_REASONS = {...}   # set of string constants
ERROR_REASONS = {...}
WARNING_REASONS: set[str] = set()

# Every module tags rows and calls sli_observe once at the end on ALL rows
sli_observe(prev_data, MODULE_NAME, start_time, trace_id)
return ExecutionResult(..., data=passed(prev_data))

# Never print(); use log_event(logger, "info"/"error", event_name, trace_id, **kw)
# Reject with reason from REJECTION_REASONS: reject(row, "WRONG_COMPANY")
```

---

## Implementation Blueprint

### Change 1 — Remove rejection_reason ChoiceQuestion; add `_derive_rejection_reason`

```python
# REMOVE from _build_questions():
questions["rejection_reason"] = ChoiceQuestion(...)   # DELETE

# ADD new helpers above _build_questions():

_OUTSIDE_UK_MARKERS = (
    "united states", "united states of america", "canada", "australia",
    "new zealand", " pa,", " tx,", " ny,", " ca,", " fl,", " va,",
    " al ", " al,",  # US state abbreviations in "city, ST," format
)

def _detect_location_country(location_strings: list[str]) -> str:
    """Return 'United States', 'United Kingdom', or '' (unknown).

    Only fires on unambiguous signals (country names or US state codes).
    Latin-script foreign cities without country suffix → return '' so the
    agent stage can decide.
    """
    lower_strings = [s.lower() for s in location_strings]
    for s in lower_strings:
        if any(m in s for m in _OUTSIDE_UK_MARKERS):
            return "United States"  # simplified; extend if needed
    for s in lower_strings:
        if "united kingdom" in s or " uk" in s or ", gb" in s:
            return "United Kingdom"
    return ""


def _derive_rejection_reason(
    answers: dict,
    asked_title_indices: list[int],
    n_locs: int,
    location_strings: list[str],
) -> str:
    """Deterministic rejection reason; called only when the row is being rejected."""
    company_ans = answers.get("company")
    if not company_ans or company_ans.noul <= _MATCH_THRESHOLD:
        return "WRONG_COMPANY"

    has_title = any(
        (a := answers.get(f"title_{i}")) and a.noul > _MATCH_THRESHOLD
        for i in asked_title_indices
    )
    if not has_title:
        return "WRONG_TITLE"

    # Company + title passed; location failed
    country = _detect_location_country(location_strings)
    if country and country != "United Kingdom":
        return "WRONG_COUNTRY"
    return "WRONG_LOCATION"
```

### Change 2 — Add `location_country` to state

```python
def _job_state(row: dict) -> dict:
    page = row.get("page") or {}
    sj = page.get("structured_job") or {}
    location_strings = row.get("location_strings") or []
    return {
        "company": row.get("resolved_company") or row.get("company") or sj.get("company") or "",
        "title":   row.get("resolved_title")  or row.get("title")   or sj.get("title")   or "",
        "location_strings": location_strings,
        "location_country": _detect_location_country(location_strings),   # NEW
        "is_remote": bool(row.get("is_remote_hint")),
        "title_tag": (page.get("title_tag") or "")[:120],
        "url": (row.get("source_url") or "")[:100],
    }
```

### Change 3 — Company pre-filter + single-candidate question

```python
# In _process_row(), BEFORE the jev call:

candidate_company = _find_matched_company(state["company"], companies)
if candidate_company is None:
    reject(row, "WRONG_COMPANY")
    return   # no jev call needed

# Build per-row questions (copy base loc+title questions, override company)
row_questions = {k: v for k, v in questions.items() if not k.startswith("company")}
row_questions["company"] = NoulQuestion(
    instructions=(
        f"Does this job page belong to '{candidate_company}'? "
        "Ignore case, a leading 'The', and legal suffixes "
        "(Ltd, plc, Group, Holdings, Corp, UK, Engineering, Systems). "
        "Consider title_tag, url, and title."
    ),
    criteria={
        "true":  f"Job belongs to '{candidate_company}'",
        "false": "Job does not belong to this company",
    },
)
```

### Change 4 — Pre-filter title questions

```python
# ADD helper:

_TITLE_SPLIT_RE = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9\s]")

def _title_word_set(text: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    words = _TITLE_SPLIT_RE.sub(" ", text.lower()).split()
    return frozenset(w.rstrip("s") for w in words if len(w) > 2)

def _relevant_title_indices(job_title: str, titles: list[str]) -> list[int]:
    """Indices of profile titles that share ≥1 word with the job title."""
    job_words = _title_word_set(job_title)
    return [
        i for i, t in enumerate(titles)
        if _title_word_set(t) & job_words
    ]

# In _process_row(), BEFORE the jev call:
asked_title_indices = _relevant_title_indices(state["title"], titles)
# Build per-row questions (remove all title_* from base, add only relevant ones)
row_questions = {k: v for k, v in row_questions.items() if not k.startswith("title_")}
for i in asked_title_indices:
    row_questions[f"title_{i}"] = questions[f"title_{i}"]
```

### Change 5 — Wire `_derive_rejection_reason` into `_process_row`

Replace the existing `rejection_reason = _get_rejection_reason(answers)` pattern:

```python
# After the jev call returns answers:

# Evaluate company (using candidate found in pre-filter)
company_ans = answers.get("company")
if not company_ans or company_ans.noul <= _MATCH_THRESHOLD:
    reject(row, _derive_rejection_reason(answers, asked_title_indices, len(locations), state["location_strings"]))
    return
# candidate_company is the canonical name (found before jev call, no need for _find_matched_company again)

matched_titles = [
    titles[i] for i in asked_title_indices
    if (a := answers.get(f"title_{i}")) and a.noul > _MATCH_THRESHOLD
]
if not matched_titles:
    reject(row, _derive_rejection_reason(answers, asked_title_indices, len(locations), state["location_strings"]))
    return

matched_locs = [
    locations[i]["name"]
    for i in range(len(locations))
    if (a := answers.get(f"loc_{i}")) and a.noul > _MATCH_THRESHOLD
]
if not matched_locs:
    reject(row, _derive_rejection_reason(answers, asked_title_indices, len(locations), state["location_strings"]))
    return

row["matched_company"]   = candidate_company   # ← use pre-computed value
row["matched_job_title"] = matched_titles
row["matched_location"]  = matched_locs
row["reason"]            = f"jev: company={candidate_company}, titles={matched_titles}, locations={matched_locs}"
row["used_llm"] = True
```

### Change 6 — Remove `_get_rejection_reason` and `ChoiceQuestion` import usage

Delete `_get_rejection_reason()` entirely.  Remove `ChoiceQuestion` from the import
if it is no longer used (check first).

## Full list of tasks (implement in order)

"""Unit tests for v2 match_jobs module — helper functions and row-level logic."""
from __future__ import annotations

import pytest
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, patch

# ── _detect_location_country ────────────────────────────────────────────────


def test_detect_country_us_from_state():
    from v2.workers.job_matcher.agent.match_jobs import _detect_location_country

    from v2.workers.job_matcher.agent.match_jobs import _detect_location_country

    assert _detect_location_country(["Birmingham"]) == ""


# ── _derive_rejection_reason ────────────────────────────────────────────────


def _make_noul_answer(noul: float):

    return NoulAnswer(noul=noul)


def test_derive_rejection_wrong_company():

    result = _derive_rejection_reason(
        answers,
        asked_title_indices=[10],
        n_locs=12,
        location_strings=["Warrington, PA, United States"],

    from v2.workers.job_matcher.agent.match_jobs import _derive_rejection_reason

**3 new issues incorporated from your analysis:**

1. **`criteria` on NoulQuestion = pure noise** (~2 280 wasted tokens per call). Every title/loc NoulQuestion currently carries `criteria={"true": "...", "false": "..."}`. That field is only meaningful for `ChoiceQuestion` — Noul only uses `instructions`. Removed from all NoulQuestion calls. Added gotcha: check if `criteria` is a required field in the dataclass before removing vs setting to `None`.

2. **Duplicate `location_strings`** (`["Warrington, PA, United States", "Warrington, PA, United States"]`). Fixed with `list(dict.fromkeys(raw_strings))` in `_job_state` — order-preserving deduplication. Added tests.

3. **`url` in company instruction is misleading**. The instruction says "Consider title_tag, url, and title" but the URL is `https://feed.example/jobs/s0001435` — no company information. Removed `url` from both the state dict and the instruction text. Added gotcha explaining when to re-add it (if production URLs ever contain company slugs).

Also noted in the PRP that **what works well** already: company 0.99, title_10 0.98, all locs 0.01–0.07 — the matching itself is sound, only the downstream processing and token efficiency need fixing.
